title: Radical Acceptance for the Unexpected
summary: A page for practicing acceptance of how early parenting differs from expectations.
goal: Use it to help a client make room for what is real while caring for themselves.
body_md: Ask what the client expected and what is true now. Practice acceptance statements and a coping step. Move gently; grief about the gap is normal and does not need fixing.

fields.label: What I expected
What is true now
A statement I can say to accept it
One thing I can do for myself today

title: Small Moments Values Practice
summary: A practice for noticing and doing small things that matter in the early months.
goal: Use it to help a client connect with values when time is short.
body_md: Look for one-minute ways to act on a value, such as a few quiet breaths with the baby or a call to a friend. The client chooses two and tries them. Review what they noticed.

fields.label: A value I care about as a parent
A one-minute action for it
When I tried it
What I noticed

title: Strengths Evidence Folder
summary: A folder-style page for collecting examples of the client's strengths in action.
goal: Use it to help a client build a concrete record of what they do well.
body_md: Ask for specific examples, not general claims. Have the client add one a day. Review for patterns across situations, and ask a trusted person to add a note if the client is willing.

fields.label: A strength I used
What happened
What it says about me
Someone who noticed

title: Inner Critic Rewrite
summary: A worksheet for catching the inner critic's lines and rewriting them.
goal: Use it to help a client respond to self-criticism with a fair view.
body_md: Collect the critic's favorite lines, then rewrite each as a fair, specific statement. Avoid forced positive thinking; the new line should be believable. Practice saying them aloud.

fields.label: The critic's line
When it shows up
A fair rewrite
How believable it feels, 0 to 100

title: Self as Context Observer Practice
summary: A practice for noticing the self that notices, apart from labels.
goal: Use it to help a client step back from labels they hold about themselves.
body_md: Guide the client to notice that they have thoughts about themselves and that something notices them. Link it to a chosen value. Keep the language plain and not abstract.

fields.label: A label I use about myself
The part of me that notices it
What changes when I notice
An action I choose anyway

title: All About Me Poster
summary: A child makes a poster of things they like, can do and are proud of.
goal: Use it to help a child see their own strengths and interests.
body_md: The child draws or pastes pictures of what they like and are good at, with help from the parent who adds one thing they admire. The poster goes in a visible spot at home.

fields.label: Things I like
Things I am good at
Something I am proud of
What my grown-up admires in me

title: Strength Cards Show and Tell
summary: Players choose strength cards that fit them and share an example.
goal: Use it to practice naming strengths with a group.
body_md: Spread strength cards on the table. Each player picks two that fit and tells a short story. The group adds one they have seen. Debrief on how it felt to hear others describe them.

fields.label: The strengths I picked
My example
One someone added
How it felt

title: Social Practice Step Ladder
summary: A ladder of social situations arranged from easy to hard.
goal: Use it to help a client plan gradual practice with social situations.
body_md: Build the list with the client and rank it by difficulty. Pick one near the bottom as the first practice. Plan what to do, not what to feel. Review how it went and move up slowly.

fields.label: Social situations I avoid
Ranking from easy to hard
The first one I will try
What I did and what happened

title: Attention Outward Experiment
summary: An experiment in shifting attention from self-monitoring to the conversation.
goal: Use it to test how shifting attention changes the experience.
body_md: Have the client try a conversation with attention on the other person, then compare with a self-focused one. Rate anxiety and how they felt afterward. Review what they noticed about the other person.

fields.label: The conversation
Where my attention was
What I noticed about the other person
How it felt compared with self-focus

title: Values in Social Moments Page
summary: A page for acting on values in social situations with anxiety along for the ride.
goal: Use it to help a client choose connection even when anxiety is present.
body_md: Ask what kind of friend or colleague the client wants to be. Choose a small social action in line with that. Rate willingness before and report what happened.

fields.label: The kind of person I want to be with others
A small social step
My willingness, 0 to 10
What happened

title: GIVE Skill Conversation Rehearsal
summary: A rehearsal for being gentle, interested, validating and easy in a conversation.
goal: Use it to practice relationship skills in a social situation.
body_md: Walk through each letter and write one line per skill. Role-play a short chat, then switch roles. Notice which skill is hardest and practice that one again.

fields.label: Gentle: what I will say
Interested: a question I will ask
Validate: what I will say
Easy manner: how I will carry myself

title: Conversation Starter Spin
summary: Players spin for a topic and practice a short chat with a partner.
goal: Use it to practice starting and keeping a conversation going.
body_md: Create a spinner with topics. Partners chat for two minutes, then swap. Debrief on what made it easier. Provide easy questions for anyone who wants a script.

fields.label: The topic I got
A question I asked
What went well
What I will try with someone I know

title: Continuing Bonds Memory Page
summary: A page for keeping connection with someone who died through memories, rituals and sayings.
goal: Use it to help a client find ways to carry a relationship forward.
body_md: Invite the client to bring a photo or object if they wish. They note memories, traditions and things the person said that they carry. Follow their pace, and let sadness be there without fixing it.

fields.label: A memory I treasure
A tradition I can keep
Something they used to say
A way I will honor them this month

title: Making Room for Grief Waves
summary: A practice for letting grief come and go while choosing small actions.
goal: Use it to help a client carry grief while moving toward values.
body_md: Name grief as waves that come with love. Practice noticing a wave, breathing, and choosing one small valued action. Do not rush the client toward acceptance; set it in their own timeline.

fields.label: What the waves feel like
What I do when a wave arrives
A value I want to honor
A small action for this week

title: Grieving Differently Together
summary: A sheet for partners who grieve in different ways to name needs and offer support.
goal: Use it to help partners understand each other's grief styles.
body_md: Each partner describes how they tend to grieve, what helps and what hurts. Avoid comparing who grieves correctly. Together they choose one shared ritual and one thing to do separately.

fields.label: Partner A: how I grieve
Partner A: what helps me
Partner B: how I grieve
Partner B: what helps me
One ritual we will share

title: Memory Box Craft
summary: A child decorates a box and fills it with drawings and small items that remind them of someone.
goal: Use it to give a child a safe place to hold memories of a loved one.
body_md: The child decorates a box and chooses items. The parent listens to stories and answers questions simply and honestly, using words like died. Plan when the box can be opened together.

fields.label: Who the box is for
What I put in it
A favorite memory
Who I can talk to when I miss them

title: Should and If Only Thought Check
summary: A thought check for if only and should thoughts that come with loss.
goal: Use it to help a client look kindly at self-blame thoughts after a loss.
body_md: List the if only thoughts and ask what the client knew at the time. Write a more compassionate view. Stay with the feeling underneath, which is often love or sorrow, rather than winning an argument.

fields.label: The if only thought
What I knew then
What I would say to a friend
A kinder way to hold it

title: Relationship Needs and Boundaries Map
summary: A map of what a client needs and where they draw lines in close relationships.
goal: Use it to help a client clarify needs and limits before a hard conversation.
body_md: Ask the client to list needs they have and ones they think they are not allowed to have. Then set limits that follow. Role-play one request so they have words ready.

fields.label: Needs I have in this relationship
Needs I hold back
A limit I want to set
How I will say it

title: Guessed Thoughts Fact Test
summary: A worksheet for testing the stories we tell about what others think.
goal: Use it to help a client check assumptions before reacting.
body_md: Ask for a recent moment when the client assumed what someone thought. List other possible explanations and what they could ask. Plan a clarifying question for real life.

fields.label: What I assumed
Other explanations
A question I could ask
What happened when I asked

title: DEAR MAN Request Builder
summary: A builder for describing, expressing, asserting, reinforcing and negotiating a request.
goal: Use it to prepare a clear, respectful request.
body_md: Walk through each letter and write one line each. Role-play the request. Notice whether the client lapses into hinting or over-explaining, then practice it again.

fields.label: Describe the situation
Express how I feel
Assert what I ask
Reinforce why it helps
What I can negotiate

title: Our Repair Moves Menu
summary: A menu where partners list the repair moves that work for them.
goal: Use it to build a shared set of ways to de-escalate and reconnect.
body_md: Each partner lists small repairs they would welcome, such as a touch, a joke or an apology. Trade menus and choose three to use. Notice which repairs the other tends to miss.

fields.label: Partner A: repair moves I welcome
Partner B: repair moves I welcome
Three we will use
How we will recognize an attempt

title: Perspective Switch Role Play
summary: Players act out a conflict from both sides and describe what each person needs.
goal: Use it to practice seeing a disagreement from another view.
body_md: Pairs choose a conflict card, play one side, then switch. Each names the other's need. Debrief on what changed in how they saw the situation. Keep the cards low-stakes.

fields.label: The conflict
The other person's need
What I noticed
What I will try next time

title: Safe Place and Support Planner
summary: A planner for naming safe places, safe people and steps for hard moments.
goal: Use it to help a survivor build present-day safety and support.
body_md: Keep work in the present: where the client feels safe, who they trust, what helps when a hard moment comes. Never ask them to write about what happened. Let them pace and choose what to share.

fields.label: A place that feels safe
People I trust
What helps in a hard moment
Who I can reach, including 988 (call or text)

title: Choosing Pace and Values Practice
summary: A practice for choosing what to do and when, guided by the client's values.
goal: Use it to affirm choice and control in a client's recovery.
body_md: Emphasize choice at every step. The client names a value, a small action and how fast they want to go. Stay in the present, and make it clear they can stop at any time.

fields.label: A value I want to live by
A small action
My pace
What I need from others

title: Grounding With the Senses Card
summary: A card with senses-based grounding steps for moments of distress.
goal: Use it to give a client a quick present-focused tool.
body_md: Practice naming things seen, heard, felt and smelled in the room. Rehearse in session at a low level of distress. Offer alternatives for clients who find closed eyes unsettling, and keep the focus on the present.

fields.label: Five things I can see
Four things I can feel
Three things I can hear
What I notice about my body now

title: My Body Is My Own Safety Chart
summary: A child draws trusted adults and a safety plan for telling when something feels wrong.
goal: Use it to help a child learn body safety and who to tell.
body_md: Use plain words and drawing. The child names trusted adults and practices saying stop and telling. If a child discloses, follow your reporting duties and the law, and stay calm and supportive. Parents get a copy of the plan.

fields.label: Grown-ups I can tell
What I can say if I feel unsafe
A safe place I can go
How I feel when I draw this

title: Partner Support and Pacing Plan
summary: A plan for a survivor and a partner to agree on pace, signals and support.
goal: Use it to help partners support intimacy and safety at the survivor's pace.
body_md: Each partner shares what helps and what they need. The survivor leads on pacing and sets signals for pausing. No details of events are needed. Rehearse a pause in session.

fields.label: Partner A: what helps me feel safe
Partner A: our signal to pause
Partner B: how I can support
Partner B: what I need for myself
How we will check in

title: Personal Coping Menu
summary: A menu of coping choices sorted by how much time and energy they need.
goal: Use it to give a client a ready list that fits their mood and the moment.
body_md: Sort strategies into quick, medium and longer, and mark which work alone and which with others. The client keeps a copy on a phone. Revisit and add as new skills are learned.

fields.label: Quick ones, under five minutes
Medium ones, up to 30 minutes
Longer ones
People I can ask for help

title: Coping Thought Cards
summary: Cards that hold a helpful thought for a hard situation.
goal: Use it to give a client a quick reminder of a helpful view.
body_md: For each hard situation, the client writes a believable coping thought on a card. Test it in role-play. Replace any that feel false or forced.

fields.label: The hard situation
The thought that helps
Where I will keep the card
How believable it is, 0 to 100

title: Distress Tolerance Skills Practice Log
summary: A log for trying a distress tolerance skill and rating the difference.
goal: Use it to practice skills before they are needed most.
body_md: Pick one skill, such as ice water or paced breathing. Rate distress before and after. Review what each skill gave the client and which ones to keep.

fields.label: The skill I tried
Distress before, 0 to 10
Distress after, 0 to 10
What I noticed

title: Spin-a-Skill Wheel Craft
summary: A child makes a wheel with coping ideas to spin when upset.
goal: Use it to give a child a playful menu of coping choices.
body_md: The child decorates a paper wheel, fills each slice with a coping idea, and spins it. The parent keeps it handy and uses it with the child at calm moments first.

fields.label: Ideas on my wheel
My favorite one
When I will spin it
Who will help me

title: Room Scavenger Skills Hunt
summary: Teams search the room for items that suggest a coping skill and explain how it helps.
goal: Use it to build a bank of coping ideas through movement and teamwork.
body_md: Teams find objects such as a soft cushion or a window and name a skill that goes with it. Share with the group. Debrief on which ideas they want in their own plan.

fields.label: The items we found
The skills they stand for
The skill I liked best
How I will use it

title: Avoidance Map
summary: A map of places, tasks and routines the client avoids because of a fear.
goal: Use it to help a client see how far avoidance reaches.
body_md: Ask the client to list what they avoid and what that costs them. Mark ones they would like back first. Choose a target and plan the first step in a later session.

fields.label: What I avoid
What it costs me
What I would like back
The first target

title: Fear Fact Sheet
summary: A sheet separating what the client believes about a feared thing from what is known.
goal: Use it to help a client check beliefs about a feared object or situation.
body_md: Write the fear, then list facts and guesses. Look at how likely and how bad the outcome would be. Keep it balanced and avoid reassurance loops. Plan a first practice step.

fields.label: The thing I fear
What I believe will happen
Facts I know
A small step to try

title: Step Toward the Fear Practice
summary: A practice for approaching a feared thing a step at a time while fear is present.
goal: Use it to help a client approach rather than avoid, guided by values.
body_md: Ask what the fear costs in valued activities. Plan a small approach step. Rate willingness before and what they did after. The aim is a life, not the absence of fear.

fields.label: What matters to me that fear gets in the way of
A small step toward it
My willingness, 0 to 10
What happened

title: Brave Explorer Passport
summary: A child collects stamps for each brave step toward a feared thing.
goal: Use it to make gradual practice feel like an adventure.
body_md: The child draws a passport and earns a stamp for each step. The parent goes first on a step, stays calm, and avoids forcing. Keep steps small and agree on them ahead of time.

fields.label: The thing I am learning to face
My first stamp
My second stamp
How I felt after

title: Fear Facing Bingo
summary: Players mark brave steps on a bingo card and share what they tried.
goal: Use it to celebrate trying brave steps in a group.
body_md: Each card has small approach steps. Players mark what they tried in the week and share. A line wins a cheer. Debrief on what helped them try.

fields.label: A brave step I took
What helped
What I noticed
The next square I want

title: Body Appreciation Letter
summary: A letter to the body thanking it for what it does for the client.
goal: Use it to help a client shift focus from appearance to what the body allows them to do.
body_md: Ask the client to write about what their body lets them do, like hugging, dancing or resting. Keep the tone kind and avoid comparison. Read a part aloud if comfortable.

fields.label: Things my body lets me do
Something it has helped me through
What I want to thank it for
One way to care for it this week

title: Comparison Trap Thought Log
summary: A log of social comparison thoughts and fairer responses.
goal: Use it to help a client notice comparing and respond with perspective.
duration: One week of logging, then 25 minutes
body_md: The client logs when they compare, what they saw and what they told themselves. Look for patterns and plan limits on triggers like feeds. Write a fair response to the top thoughts.

fields.label: Where I was when I compared
What I told myself
What the comparison leaves out
A fairer thought

title: Values Beyond Appearance Practice
summary: A practice that connects the client's values to choices that have nothing to do with how they look.
goal: Use it to help a client spend time on what matters instead of appearance.
body_md: Ask what the client would do with the time and attention they spend on how they look. Choose a value and a step. Review what they noticed about pulling their attention away.

fields.label: What I give attention to about my looks
What matters to me more
A step toward it
What I noticed

title: Mirror Mindfulness Practice
summary: A mindfulness practice of describing the self in the mirror without judgment.
goal: Use it to build non-judgmental awareness while looking at oneself.
body_md: Guide the client to describe what they see in neutral words, noticing judgments and letting them go. Keep it brief and stop if distress rises. Pair with a calming skill.

fields.label: Neutral words I used
Judgments I noticed
How I let them go
What I felt afterward

title: Superpower Self Portrait
summary: A child draws a self-portrait with captions for what their body and mind can do.
goal: Use it to help a child value what they can do.
body_md: The child draws themself and labels strengths such as running or helping. The parent adds a caption about character. Model kind talk about bodies at home, and avoid comments on looks.

fields.label: What I can do
A kind thing I do
What my grown-up admires
My superpower

title: Weekly Energy Ledger
summary: A one-week sheet where a client lists activities and rates what each gives or costs in energy.
goal: Use it to help a client see where energy goes and plan a steadier week.
body_md: Have the client fill in two or three days in session so the ratings feel concrete. Look for the activities that cost a lot and give nothing back, and for ones that refill them. Plan one small swap together instead of overhauling the week.

fields.label: Activities that took a lot of energy this week
Activities that gave energy back
One thing I could move, shorten or share
One refilling thing I will add this week

title: Unsent Letter Template
summary: A structured page for writing a letter to someone the client will not send, with a closing step to put it away.
goal: Use it to give a client a contained place to say what has gone unsaid.
body_md: Offer this when a client carries words they cannot say to someone. Frame it as writing for themselves, with no plan to send. Agree beforehand how the letter will be kept or let go of, and leave time to check in on how they feel afterward.

fields.label: Who the letter is to
What I wish they knew
What I needed from them
What I want to say to close it
How I will put this letter away

title: Decision Values Compass
summary: A one-page sheet for weighing a decision against what matters most to the client.
goal: Use it to help a client check a choice against their own values.
body_md: Useful when a client is stuck between two reasonable options. Ask them to name values first, then compare each option against them. The sheet does not choose for them; it makes the trade-offs visible so they can decide.

fields.label: The decision I am facing
Three things that matter most to me here
How option one fits those
How option two fits those
What I notice when I read both
The smallest next step

title: Boundary Sentence Workshop
summary: A fill-in page for drafting a short, kind boundary statement and a follow-through plan.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare words and actions for a boundary.
body_md: Clients often know the boundary but freeze on the wording. Draft the sentence together, then rehearse it aloud. Spend time on the follow-through line, since the plan for what they will do matters as much as the sentence.

fields.label: The situation where I need a boundary
What I am willing and not willing to do
My boundary in one sentence
What I will do if it is crossed
Who can back me up

title: Sleep Wind-Down Log
summary: A seven-night log of evening habits, wind-down steps and how settled the client felt at bedtime.
goal: Use it to help a client spot which evening habits ease their way into sleep.
body_md: This is a plain log of habits, not a sleep program. Review it for patterns such as screens, caffeine timing or racing thoughts at bedtime. Pick one habit to adjust and keep the rest steady so the change is easy to read.

fields.label: What I did in the last hour before bed
What helped me settle
What kept me wired
How settled I felt at lights out
One change to try tomorrow night

title: Cost of Thinking Traps Ledger
summary: A two-column ledger comparing what a recurring thought costs a client with what it gives.
goal: Use it to help a client weigh the usefulness of a thought, not only its truth.
body_md: Some thoughts are hard to disprove but plainly unhelpful. Ask what believing it buys and what it costs, then ask what a more useful stance might be. Keep the tone curious and avoid arguing with the client.

fields.label: A thought that keeps coming back
What this thought gets me
What this thought costs me
A more useful way to hold it
What I would do differently

title: Worst, Best, Most Likely Chart
summary: A three-row chart for predicting the worst, best and most likely outcome of a worry, then checking later.
goal: Use it to help a client widen a narrow prediction and compare it with what happened.
body_md: Fill in the three rows in session, then have the client rate how much they believe each. After the event, review what really happened. Pay attention to how often the most likely outcome was ordinary and manageable.

fields.label: The situation I am worried about
Worst outcome and how much I believe it
Best outcome and how much I believe it
Most likely outcome and how much I believe it
What actually happened
What I take from the comparison

title: Thought Distance Exercise
summary: A page of steps for stepping back from a thought by changing how it is worded and viewed.
goal: Use it to help a client treat a thought as a mental event, not a fact.
body_md: Walk the client through rewording the thought as 'I am having the thought that...' and then picturing it from farther away. Ask what changes. This works best on one specific thought, not a whole worry theme.

fields.label: The thought, written as it comes
The thought reworded with 'I am having the thought that'
How strongly I believe it now
What I notice with more distance
What I want to do next

title: Belief Test Planning Page
summary: A planning sheet to test one belief through a small, specific action and record what happens.
goal: Use it to help a client turn a belief into something they can test.
body_md: Choose a belief the client holds firmly and a test small enough to carry out this week. Agree on what they predict and how they will know. Debrief the result with the client's own words and avoid steering toward a lesson.

fields.label: The belief I want to test
My prediction and how sure I am
The experiment: what, where, when
What I will watch for
What happened
What this tells me about the belief

title: Mood Lifters Menu
summary: A menu of small activities sorted by effort, with a column for the mood before and after.
goal: Use it to help a client link small actions with shifts in mood.
body_md: Build the menu with the client from their own interests, sorted into tiny, easy and bigger. Ask them to rate mood before and after. Review the ratings with curiosity about which actions helped, and drop any that felt like chores.

fields.label: Tiny actions I could do in five minutes
Easy actions I could do in an hour
Bigger actions I could plan for the weekend
Mood before and after what I tried
What I want more of

title: Bus Passengers Role Walkthrough
summary: A walk-through of the passengers-on-the-bus metaphor with a client's own difficult thoughts as passengers.
goal: Use it to help a client keep driving toward their values with noisy thoughts aboard.
body_md: Have the client name the loudest passengers and the direction they want to drive. Act out the metaphor if the client is willing. The point is that passengers can shout while the client still steers, not that they must quiet down.

fields.label: The direction I want to drive my life
The passengers that shout the loudest
What they tell me to do
What I can do while they keep talking
One turn I will make this week

title: Values and Actions Gap Review
summary: A table comparing how much a value matters with how much time the client gave it this week.
goal: Use it to help a client find where their days and values drift apart.
body_md: Choose three or four values and ask for honest ratings of importance and recent action. A gap is information, not failure. Pick the one the client cares most about and plan a very small action toward it.

fields.label: Value one and my action this week
Value two and my action this week
Value three and my action this week
The biggest gap I notice
A small step I will take

title: Hands as Thoughts Defusion Demo
summary: An in-session demo where the client holds their hands over their face, then lowers them to see the room.
goal: Use it to give a client a felt sense of thoughts getting in the way of seeing.
body_md: Ask the client to cover their face with their hands as if they were thoughts, notice what they can do, then lower the hands slowly. Ask what changed. It is a short demo and should be followed by a short talk about what thoughts do and do not do.

fields.label: What it was like with hands over my face
What it was like with hands in my lap
A thought that sits like my hands do
What I could do while the thought is near
What I noticed afterward

title: Willingness Rating Sheet
summary: A rating page for how willing a client is to feel the discomfort that comes with a valued action.
goal: Use it to help a client choose how much discomfort they will carry toward something that matters.
body_md: Ask for the valued action and the discomfort that comes with it, then a willingness rating from zero to ten. Explore what a slightly higher number would take. Respect a low number and ask what would make a smaller action possible.

fields.label: The action that matters to me
The discomfort that comes with it
My willingness from 0 to 10
What would make it a point higher
What I will try this week

title: Present Moment Anchors Card
summary: A pocket card for noticing five things in the room and returning attention to what the client is doing.
goal: Use it to help a client come back to the present during a busy day.
body_md: Practice the anchors in session first so the card is familiar. Clients can write their own anchors, such as a sound or the feel of the chair. Keep it short and treat wandering attention as the normal reason to practice.

fields.label: Five things I can see
Three sounds I can hear
One thing I can feel under my hands
A place in my day where I will try this
How it felt to pause

title: Pros and Cons of Urge Acting Sheet
summary: A DBT pros-and-cons grid for acting on an urge versus using a skill, filled in during calm.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare a reason to choose a skill before a strong urge.
body_md: Complete the grid in a calm moment and keep it handy for hard ones. Include both short-term and long-term pros and cons. Clients often skip the short-term pros of the urge, and naming them honestly makes the sheet more believable.

fields.label: The urge or behavior I am weighing
Pros of acting on it
Cons of acting on it
Pros of using a skill instead
Cons of using a skill
My choice for next time

title: Describe and Label Emotions Worksheet
summary: A worksheet for naming an emotion by its prompt, body cues, urges and aftermath.
goal: Use it to help a client describe an emotion in full without acting on it.
body_md: Take one recent emotion and walk through the prompting event, interpretation, body sensations, urge and what followed. Ask the client to stick to what an observer could see, then separate the story from the facts.

fields.label: What happened just before
What I told myself about it
What I felt in my body
What I wanted to do
What I did and what followed

title: Open Palms Posture Practice
summary: A short practice for relaxing the body toward acceptance, with space to note what shifts.
goal: Use it to help a client soften toward a situation they cannot change right now.
body_md: Teach the posture in session: palms open, shoulders loose, a half-smile if it comes. Pair it with a single hard situation and ask for a note on what changes. It is a body cue for acceptance and does not mean the client approves.

fields.label: The situation I am fighting
What my body does when I resist
What I notice with open hands
A sentence I can say to myself
When I will practice this

title: Interpersonal Priorities Rating
summary: A rating sheet that helps a client weigh the goal, the relationship and self-respect in a request.
goal: Use it to help a client pick how firmly to ask in a situation.
body_md: Walk through the three priorities with a real request and have the client rate each from one to ten. Then decide together whether to lean on DEAR MAN, GIVE or FAST more heavily. Different ratings lead to different approaches.

fields.label: What I want from this situation
How important the goal is, 1 to 10
How important the relationship is, 1 to 10
How important my self-respect is, 1 to 10
The approach I will take

title: Daily Wise Mind Check-In
summary: A brief daily check-in to notice emotion mind, reasonable mind and what wise mind says.
goal: Use it to help a client practice reaching for wise mind each day.
body_md: Ask for one entry a day tied to a small decision. Look in session for where the client already finds wise mind and where they overlook it. Keep entries short so the habit sticks.

fields.label: The situation today
What emotion mind says
What reasonable mind says
What wise mind says
What I did

title: Weekly State of Us Meeting Agenda
summary: A shared agenda for a short weekly talk covering appreciation, chores, concerns and plans.
goal: Use it to give a couple a steady, low-pressure time to talk about the relationship.
body_md: Each partner fills in their own column beforehand and brings it. Start with appreciation, end with something to look forward to, and keep concerns to one each. Model it in session before they try it at home.

fields.label: Partner A: one thing I appreciated this week
Partner B: one thing I appreciated this week
Partner A: one concern, said gently
Partner B: one concern, said gently
Something we will plan together

title: Repair Attempt Phrase Bank
summary: Each partner lists phrases that help them reconnect after a hard exchange.
goal: Use it to help a couple agree on repair words that actually land.
body_md: Have each partner write phrases that would help them soften, then trade lists. Ask what they would actually say in the heat of it. Pick two phrases each to try and review in the next session how they were received.

fields.label: Partner A: words that help me soften
Partner B: words that help me soften
Words that would make it worse
Two phrases we will each try
How we will let each other know it worked

title: Planning Load Balance Check
summary: A planning sheet for comparing each partner's commitments and who carries the logistics.
goal: Use it to help a couple see and rebalance the invisible planning work.
body_md: Have each partner list recurring tasks and who plans, remembers and does them. Many couples find that planning is the uneven part. Stay neutral and help them choose one task to hand over completely.

fields.label: Partner A: tasks I plan or remember
Partner B: tasks I plan or remember
Where it feels uneven
One task we will hand over completely
When we will check in again

title: Appreciation Jar Cards
summary: A set of cards where partners write short notes on what they valued about each other this week.
goal: Use it to help a couple notice and say the good they otherwise let pass.
body_md: Ask the couple to write one card each a day and read them aloud at the weekend. Specific notes work better than general ones. If one partner feels awkward, start with two a week and build from there.

fields.label: Partner A: something B did that I valued
Partner B: something A did that I valued
A small moment we shared this week
A thank-you I have not said yet
What it was like to hear the notes

title: Different Needs Translation Sheet
summary: Partners write what they asked for, what they needed underneath, and what they could ask instead.
goal: Use it to help a couple move from complaint to a clear request.
body_md: Take one recurring complaint and have each partner translate it into a need and a doable request. Practice stating the request in one calm sentence. Watch for requests hidden inside criticism and name them kindly.

fields.label: Partner A: my complaint
Partner A: the need under it
Partner B: my complaint
Partner B: the need under it
A request each of us can make

title: Feelings Weather Station
summary: A child draws today's feelings as weather and builds a small forecast with a parent.
goal: Use it to help a child name feelings through a picture they can share.
body_md: The child draws sun, clouds or storms for how they feel and gives a forecast for tomorrow. The parent listens, repeats back what they see, and does not fix. Post the drawing where the child can add a new one each day.

fields.label: Today my feelings are like this weather
What made the weather change
What helps a storm pass
My forecast for tomorrow

title: Settling Glitter Jar Craft
summary: A child makes a glitter jar with a parent and learns to watch it settle while breathing slowly.
goal: Use it to give a child a visual, hands-on way to slow down.
body_md: Make the jar together with water, glue and glitter, sealed tightly. Explain that the glitter settles like busy thoughts and shake it only when the child chooses. The parent practices with the child at calm times, not only upsets.

fields.label: Colors I picked and why
What it looks like when I am upset
How the jar looks when it settles
Where we will keep the jar

title: Brave Steps Ladder Drawing
summary: A child draws a staircase and places small brave steps on each stair with stickers.
goal: Use it to help a child plan small steps toward something hard.
body_md: The child draws the staircase and picks something they want to do, then you and the parent break it into small steps. The parent cheers effort and does not push past the step. Add stickers as each stair is tried.

fields.label: The big brave thing I want to do
First tiny step at the bottom
Next step up
The top stair
Who will cheer me on

title: Kindness Tree Collage
summary: A child builds a paper tree and adds a leaf each time they notice or give kindness.
goal: Use it to help a child notice kind things they and others do.
body_md: The child cuts out a trunk and adds a leaf with a short note each day. The parent writes the words for younger children. At the end of the week, count the leaves together and talk about which one felt best.

fields.label: A kind thing I did
A kind thing someone did for me
How it felt
A leaf I want to add tomorrow

title: Worry Monster Feeding Box
summary: A child decorates a box for worries, writes or draws them, and feeds the monster at a set time.
goal: Use it to give a child a place to put worries and a time to let them go.
body_md: The child decorates the box and picks a time of day to feed it. Worries go in, and the parent does not rescue or lecture, only listens briefly. Check the contents with the child once a week and decide what to do with each.

fields.label: What my worry monster looks like
A worry I fed it today
What the monster says back
What I do while it eats
What I want to tell it

title: Two Truths and a Wish Feelings Round
summary: Players share two true things and one wish about a recent feeling, and others guess the wish.
goal: Use it to help a group share feelings through a light, familiar format.
body_md: Each player offers two true things and one wish about their week. Others guess the wish, then the speaker reveals it. Debrief on what it was like to share and to be guessed. Keep the pace light and let anyone pass.

fields.label: My two true things
My wish
What I learned about someone else
What it was like to share

title: Skill Charades
summary: Players act out a coping skill without words while others guess it, then say when they might use it.
goal: Use it to help a group remember coping skills through movement and laughter.
body_md: Write skills on cards such as breathing, grounding, asking for help and taking a break. Players take turns acting them out. After each guess, the actor says when they could use it. Debrief on which skill felt most doable.

fields.label: Skills I acted or guessed
A skill I forgot I had
A moment this week I could use one
The skill I will try first

title: Pass the Compliment Circle
summary: Players pass a ball and give the next person a specific, true compliment about what they do.
goal: Use it to help a group practice giving and receiving kind words.
body_md: Sit in a circle and pass a soft ball. The holder gives a specific compliment about an action, not looks. The receiver says thank you without deflecting. Debrief on how it felt to receive and what made some compliments land.

fields.label: A compliment I gave
A compliment I received
What it was like to say thank you
A compliment I want to give this week

title: Options Brainstorm Relay
summary: Teams race to brainstorm solutions to a card-based problem and then pick one together.
goal: Use it to help a group practice generating options before choosing.
body_md: Teams get a problem card and a minute to list ideas, with no judging. They then pick one and say why. Debrief on how it felt to hold off judgment and on which options surprised them. Use client-made problem cards if they are willing.

fields.label: Our problem card
Ideas we listed
The idea we chose and why
What I learned about options

title: Mindful Minute Challenge
summary: Players try to stay focused on one simple object for a minute and compare what they noticed.
goal: Use it to help a group practice attention in a playful, low-stakes way.
body_md: Hand each player an object such as a stone or a leaf. For one minute, they notice everything about it. Compare notes. Wandering is expected and counts as part of the game. Debrief on what pulled attention away and how they came back.

fields.label: What I noticed about my object
What pulled my attention away
How I came back
Where I could try this in daily life

title: Safe Cues Inventory
summary: A sheet for listing places, people and objects that feel safe, with senses for each.
goal: Use it to help a client build a store of safety cues for grounding.
body_md: This stays on the present and on what feels safe now. Invite the client to include real and imagined places and note the senses involved. Do not ask for details of past events. Pace the session and stop if the client feels pulled out of the present.

fields.label: A place that feels safe, real or imagined
What I see, hear and feel there
A person or pet who helps me feel safe
An object I can hold when I need steadiness
How I can bring one of these into my day

title: Stuck Point Notes for Today
summary: A short log that lets a client name a current belief that feels stuck and look at it with support.
goal: Use it to help a client notice stuck beliefs about safety or trust without retelling events.
body_md: Keep the focus on the belief as it shows up today, such as 'I can't trust anyone'. Ask what supports it and what a more balanced version might be. Do not ask for the story behind it as homework; work with the thought only.

fields.label: A belief that keeps showing up
How much I believe it right now
What supports it
What does not fit it
A more balanced way to say it

title: Anchoring Skills Ladder
summary: A ladder of distress tolerance skills ordered from lightest to strongest for intense moments.
goal: Use it to help a client choose a grounding skill that fits the strength of the moment.
body_md: Build the ladder with the client in a calm moment, from noticing five things to cold water or movement. Rehearse the top rung only if the client agrees and the setting is safe. Keep a copy where it is easy to reach.

fields.label: Light skills I can use when a wave is small
Medium skills for when it builds
Strong skills for the hardest moments
Who I can contact for support
Which rung I will rehearse this week

title: Present and Safe Reminder Cards
summary: Cards a client writes with true statements about the present and a value they are moving toward.
goal: Use it to help a client return to the present and to what they care about.
body_md: Write cards in the session such as 'Right now I am here and I am safe in this room' only if the client finds them true. Pair each with a value-based action. Review which cards help and drop any that feel forced.

fields.label: A true sentence about this moment
A value that matters to me
A small action toward that value
Where I will keep these cards
How I will know the cards are helping

title: Grounding Scavenger Hunt
summary: A paced game where players find objects by color, texture and sound to anchor in the present.
goal: Use it to help clients practice grounding through a light and structured game.
body_md: Call out categories such as something soft, something blue or a sound you can hear. Players find or name one. Keep to the present and never ask about past events. Debrief on which category settled them most and stop whenever someone needs a break.

fields.label: The category that helped me most
Something soft I found
A sound I noticed
How my body feels now
When I could use this at home

title: Worry Window Planner
summary: A weekly page for scheduling a short worry time and parking worries until then.
goal: Use it to help a client contain worry to a set window.
body_md: Agree on a daily fifteen-minute window and a place to jot worries during the day. In worry time, sort each worry into one that can be acted on and one that cannot. Review in session how many were left and what changed.

fields.label: My worry time each day
Worries I parked today
Worries I can act on, and the first step
Worries I cannot act on, and what I will do instead
What I noticed after a week

title: What If Then What Chain
summary: A chain that follows a 'what if' worry forward to the next steps the client could take.
goal: Use it to help a client move from a catastrophic question to a coping plan.
body_md: Write the worry, then ask 'and then what?' until the client reaches a point they could cope with or act on. Notice where the chain stops being likely. End with one thing they would do if it came true.

fields.label: My 'what if' worry
And then what happens?
And then what?
How likely each step is, 0 to 100
What I would do if it happened
What I want to remember

title: Anxiety as Weather Practice
summary: A practice for watching anxious feelings like weather while taking a valued action.
goal: Use it to help a client carry anxious feelings without waiting for them to leave.
body_md: Name the feelings as weather passing overhead and ask the client to keep going with a valued task. Ask what it was like to let the weather be. The point is the action, and weather changing is a bonus, not the goal.

fields.label: The weather in me right now
A valued action I want to take
What I did while the weather stayed
What I noticed when I stopped fighting it
What I will try again

title: Worry Dragon Drawing
summary: A child draws a worry dragon, gives it a name and decides how to politely tell it to wait.
goal: Use it to help a child step back from worries by giving them a shape.
body_md: The child draws the dragon and writes what it says. The parent listens, then helps the child try a line such as 'Thanks, dragon, I'll check later'. Avoid lengthy reassurance; short, calm replies work better.

fields.label: My dragon looks like this
What my dragon says
What I say back
What I do while the dragon is loud
Who helps me

title: Partner Support Plan for Anxious Moments
summary: Partners agree on how to help when anxiety is high, what helps and what does not.
goal: Use it to help a couple settle on a supportive response to anxiety.
body_md: Have the anxious partner say what helps and what feels like pressure, and the other say what they can offer. Watch for reassurance that keeps worry going. End with one agreed phrase and one agreed action.

fields.label: Partner A: when anxiety is high, I need
Partner A: what does not help
Partner B: what I can offer
A phrase we will use
How we will review this

title: Small Wins Record
summary: A daily record of tiny things done, however small, with a short note about how each felt.
goal: Use it to help a client notice what they are doing when everything feels like too much.
body_md: Define a win generously: getting out of bed, a shower, a short reply. Ask for three a day. Review the list together without adding pressure, and look at which wins gave a little lift.

fields.label: Three small things I did today
Which one felt best
What made it possible
One tiny thing for tomorrow
If my mood feels unsafe, I can call or text 988

title: Evidence for the Quiet Voice
summary: A thought record for the harsh inner voice, with a column for kinder, accurate replies.
goal: Use it to help a client check a harsh thought and write a fairer one.
body_md: Choose one harsh thought from the week and run the evidence for and against it. Ask what they would say to a friend. Keep the new thought believable; a small shift is better than a forced positive.

fields.label: The situation
The harsh thought
Evidence for it
Evidence against it
What I would say to a friend
A fairer thought

title: Values in Low Energy Days
summary: A menu of values-based actions sized to low, medium and higher energy.
goal: Use it to help a client keep acting on values when energy is low.
body_md: Draw three columns for energy and fill each with actions linked to values, such as texting a friend or watering a plant. Ask the client to pick by the day's energy, not by guilt. Revisit which items are realistic.

fields.label: A value I care about
A tiny action when energy is low
An action when energy is medium
An action when energy is higher
Which one I will do today

title: Build Mastery and Pleasant Events Plan
summary: A weekly plan with one mastery action and one pleasant event each day.
goal: Use it to help a client balance accomplishment with enjoyment.
body_md: Choose one mastery action and one pleasant event per day, both small enough to be done on a hard day. Review whether they happened and how they felt. Adjust difficulty up or down based on the week.

fields.label: Mastery action I will do each day
Pleasant event I will do each day
What got in the way
How I felt afterward
What I will change next week

title: Low Mood and Closeness Conversation
summary: Partners talk about what low mood is like and how to stay connected without pressure.
goal: Use it to help a couple talk about low mood without blame.
body_md: Invite the person with low mood to say what they would like from their partner on hard days, and the partner to share what they need too. Avoid problem-solving too early. Agree on one small way to connect each day.

fields.label: Partner A: what low days feel like to me
Partner B: what I notice and feel
What helps us stay close
What we need from each other
One small daily connection

title: Task Launch Pad
summary: A sheet that breaks a dreaded task into a first two-minute step, a timer and a reward.
goal: Use it to help a client start a task that feels hard to begin.
body_md: Pick one task the client has been avoiding and shrink the first step until it is almost silly. Add a timer and a small reward afterward. Review whether starting got easier and what made it so.

fields.label: The task I keep putting off
The two-minute first step
How long I will set the timer for
My reward when I start
What got in the way

title: Time Blindness Estimator
summary: A log comparing estimated and actual task time to calibrate planning.
goal: Use it to help a client plan with more realistic time estimates.
body_md: Ask the client to guess task times, then record real times for a week. Look at the gap and add a buffer. Many clients find the gap steady, which makes planning easier. Avoid judgment about speed.

fields.label: The task
My time guess
How long it really took
The gap
The buffer I will add next time

title: Body Doubling Craft Table
summary: A child and parent work side by side on their own tasks with a visual timer and a stamp card.
goal: Use it to help a child get through a task with someone nearby.
body_md: The parent sits with the child at a table, each with their own task, and sets a visual timer. A stamp goes on the card after each round. Keep rounds short and praise starting, not only finishing.

fields.label: The task I am working on
How long I will work
How I felt when the timer ended
What helped me stay going
What I will do for a break

title: Impulse Brake Freeze Game
summary: Players move to music and freeze on a signal, then name the pause and what they chose next.
goal: Use it to help clients practice noticing and holding a pause.
body_md: Play music and call freeze. Players hold still and name something they notice, then choose a new action. Vary the signal so it is not predictable. Debrief on the pause, what it took, and where in real life it could help.

fields.label: What I noticed while frozen
What was hardest about the pause
A moment this week I could pause
What I will try next

title: Household Systems Reset
summary: Partners build one shared system for a recurring chore, with reminders that don't feel like nagging.
goal: Use it to help a couple replace reminders with a shared system.
body_md: Choose one chore that causes friction. Agree on a visible system such as a shared list or a fixed time, and how reminders will be sent and received. Name the tone you each prefer. Revisit after two weeks.

fields.label: The chore that causes friction
Partner A: how I like reminders
Partner B: how I like reminders
The system we will try
How we will check in

title: Urge Log and Pattern Finder
summary: A log of urges for substance use with time, place, trigger, intensity and what the client did.
goal: Use it to help a client see patterns in urges and the choices they made.
body_md: Ask for brief entries and stress that urges noted are not failures. Look for repeating times, places and feelings, and ask what worked even once. Pick one pattern and plan a change together.

fields.label: When and where the urge came
What was going on
How strong it was, 0 to 10
What I did
What helped, even a little

title: Urge Thoughts Reality Check
summary: A thought record for the thoughts that come with an urge for substance use.
goal: Use it to help a client examine urge thoughts like 'just once will be fine'.
body_md: Write the exact thought and ask what it promises and what has really followed in the past. Build a response the client believes. Keep the stance nonjudgmental and let the client define their own goal.

fields.label: The urge thought
What it promises
What happened last time
A response I believe
What I will do next

title: Urge Surfing with Values
summary: A practice for noticing an urge rise and fall while holding a value in mind.
goal: Use it to help a client ride out an urge while staying connected to what matters.
body_md: Guide the client to watch the urge like a wave, noting body sensations, and to name a value as they do. Practice in session with a mild urge first. The aim is to build room between urge and action.

fields.label: Where I feel the urge in my body
How it changed over a few minutes
A value I held in mind
What I did next
Where I will practice

title: Alternate Rebellion and Adaptive Denial Plan
summary: A plan that lists safe alternatives for urges and ways to put a decision on hold.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare skills for moments when urges arise.
body_md: Fill in alternative actions and ways to delay a decision, such as a timer or a call. Rehearse one in session. Add a line about who to contact for support. Substance use and urges are the focus, never the person.

fields.label: My most common urge moments
Safe alternatives I can try
How I will delay the decision
Who I can contact
Support available any time, including 988 by call or text

title: Supporting Change Together Agreement
summary: Partners agree on how to support a goal around substance use without monitoring or blame.
goal: Use it to help a couple build a supportive plan around substance use.
body_md: Have the partner with the goal say what support looks like and the other say what they need. Discuss what to do after a hard day or a lapse. Focus on shared plans and avoid blame.

fields.label: Partner A: my goal and what helps
Partner B: what I can offer and what I need
What we will do on hard days
What we will do after a lapse
When we will check in

title: Anger Cue Map
summary: A body outline where a client marks early signs of anger and numbers them by order of arrival.
goal: Use it to help a client catch anger earlier.
body_md: Have the client color or mark where anger shows up in the body and in what order. Then ask for the earliest cue and when they might have stepped away. Practice naming the cue aloud.

fields.label: Where I feel anger first
What comes next
My earliest cue
What I can do at the first cue
Someone who can help me notice

title: Hot Thought Slowdown
summary: A thought record focused on the quick interpretation behind an angry moment.
goal: Use it to help a client slow down the interpretation behind anger.
body_md: Take a recent angry moment and slow it down: trigger, the thought, the feeling, the action. Ask what else could be true. The aim is a wider range of interpretations, not to deny that anger happened.

fields.label: What happened
What I told myself
What I felt and did
Another way to see it
What I would like to do next time

title: Opposite Action for Anger Worksheet
summary: A worksheet that plans opposite action for anger urges when anger doesn't fit the facts.
goal: Use it to help a client choose a different action when anger is not helpful.
body_md: Check the facts first and decide with the client whether anger fits. If not, plan gentle avoidance, kind actions and a softer posture. This is a skill for some moments, not a rule to suppress anger.

fields.label: Situation
Do the facts fit my anger?
My urge
An opposite action
How it went

title: Paper Volcano Cool-Down Build
summary: A child builds a paper volcano and draws what happens before, during and after it erupts.
goal: Use it to help a child notice anger building and choose a cool-down.
body_md: The child builds or draws the volcano and marks small signs of heat at the base. The parent helps pick two cool-downs and practices them at calm times. Praise the choice to cool down, not only success.

fields.label: How my volcano starts to warm up
What it looks like when it erupts
Two things I can do to cool down
What my grown-up can do
Where we will keep this

title: Cool Down Cards Game
summary: Players draw cards for tense situations and act out calming choices, then compare choices.
goal: Use it to help a group practice calm responses to common triggers.
body_md: Deal situation cards such as a teasing comment or a lost game. Each player picks a calm choice and acts it out in turns. Others guess. Debrief on what made the choice difficult and which options felt most doable.

fields.label: The situation I drew
The calm choice I tried
What made it hard
What I might use in real life

title: Compulsion Time Tracker
summary: A weekly tracker of time spent on rituals and the situations that set them off.
goal: Use it to help a client see how much time rituals take.
body_md: Ask the client to note roughly how long rituals last and what came before. The aim is awareness, not stopping yet. Look together for the biggest time costs and discuss what they might choose to work on first.

fields.label: The trigger
The ritual
About how long it took
How anxious I felt before and after
What I noticed over the week

title: Uncertainty Practice Ladder
summary: A ladder of situations where the client practices tolerating not knowing, ordered by difficulty.
goal: Use it to help a client plan graded practice with uncertainty.
body_md: Build the ladder with the client, starting with items that feel manageable. Agree on the response to practice, such as leaving a task unchecked. Review in session how each step went, and move at their pace.

fields.label: Step on my ladder
How hard it is, 0 to 10
What I will do and not do
What happened
The next step

title: Thoughts Are Not Instructions Practice
summary: A practice for noticing an intrusive thought and choosing the next action by value.
goal: Use it to help a client separate a thought from what they do next.
body_md: Have the client name the thought as 'I'm having the thought that...' and ask what they would like to do with their time. Explain that the thought can stay. Practice with a mild thought first.

fields.label: The intrusive thought
How I name it
What the thought urges me to do
What I choose to do instead
A value behind that choice

title: OCD Bully Naming Drawing
summary: A child draws and names the 'bossy worry', and a parent practices a short, calm reply.
goal: Use it to help a child see worry as separate and plan not to obey it.
body_md: The child draws the bossy worry and writes what it demands. The parent and child practice a short reply such as 'I won't do that today'. The parent avoids giving extra reassurance or joining rituals.

fields.label: What my bossy worry looks like
What it tells me to do
What I say back
What my grown-up will do
A brave thing I did

title: Reassurance and Accommodation Agreement
summary: Partners agree on kind ways to answer repeated questions and rituals without feeding them.
goal: Use it to help a couple change how they respond to reassurance requests.
body_md: Review which requests the partner currently answers and how it feels for each person. Agree on a supportive script and a gradual change. Practice the script and emphasize shared goals, not criticism.

fields.label: Partner A: the questions or rituals I ask for help with
Partner B: how I respond now
What we will try instead

title: Panic Wave Notes
summary: A record of what happened before, during and after a panic attack and what helped it pass.
goal: Use it to help a client see the shape and pattern of panic.
body_md: Fill in after each episode with brief notes. Look for triggers, timing and what the client did. Notice that the wave rose and fell, and ask what helped even slightly. Don't search for a single cause.

title: Body Sensation Interpretation Sheet
summary: A sheet that lists body sensations, the scary interpretation and a calmer, accurate one.
goal: Use it to help a client rethink what body sensations mean in a panic wave.
body_md: List sensations such as a racing heart and the feared meaning, then work out other explanations that fit. Rehearse the calmer statement aloud. Encourage checking with a medical professional for any physical concern.

fields.label: A sensation I notice
What I fear it means
Other explanations that fit

title: Making Room for the Wave Practice
summary: A practice for letting panic sensations rise and fall while staying with a chosen action.
goal: Use it to help a client make room for sensations instead of fighting them.
body_md: Teach the client to notice, breathe into and make room for the sensation, then keep doing what they were doing. Practice with a mild sensation first. Debrief on what changed when they stopped fighting.

fields.label: Where I feel it

title: TIPP Cheat Card for Surges
summary: A pocket card describing temperature, intense exercise, paced breathing and relaxation for surges.
goal: Use it to help a client use body-based skills to bring arousal down.
body_md: Walk through each step and practice paced breathing in session. Discuss safety with cold water or intense exercise and adjust to the client's health. The client writes which steps they would use first.

title: Heart Racing Body Drawing
summary: A child draws what happens in their body during big scared feelings and colors a calm-down path.
goal: Use it to help a child understand body signals and plan to calm.
body_md: The child colors where they feel scared feelings and draws a path to calm with steps. The parent practices slow breathing alongside, like blowing bubbles. Keep the explanations simple and warm.

fields.label: Where my body feels the scared feeling
What it does

Who helps me

title: Ten-Minute Play Plan
summary: A weekly plan for short, child-led play with no phones and no teaching.
goal: Use it to help a parent build warm connection with a child.
body_md: Suggest ten minutes a day of child-led play with the parent describing and praising instead of directing. Record how it went. Many parents find it hard not to correct, so plan for that.

fields.label: When special time will happen
What my child chose
What I said that helped
What was hard
What I will do again

title: Parent Hot Thought Check
summary: A thought record for the quick judgments a parent makes in tense moments.

title: Noticing the Hook Log
summary: A log for catching the moments a thought or feeling pulls the client away from what matters.
goal: Use it to help a client spot hooks and choose what to do next.
body_md: Introduce the idea of being hooked, then have the client log a few moments across the week. Review for patterns in hooks, such as criticism or fatigue. Ask what a values-guided response would have looked like, without blaming the times they got pulled.

title: Committed Action Mini-Goals Sheet
summary: A sheet that turns one value into three small goals with a time and a likely obstacle.
goal: Use it to help a client move from knowing their values to taking small steps.
body_md: Start with one value the client chose and turn it into goals they could finish within a week. Make each one specific enough to picture: when, where, how long. Name the obstacle that will most likely show up and plan a willing response.

title: Four-Quadrant ACT Matrix Page
summary: A two-by-two page sorting what the client moves toward, what hooks them and what they notice inside.
goal: Use it to give a client a simple map of away moves, toward moves and inner experience.
body_md: Draw the matrix with the client and fill in the lower half first, what they notice inside and what they do to get away from it. Then fill in who and what matter to them. Look together at which moves go toward the right side and which away.

fields.label: Who and what matter to me

title: Behavior Chain Mapping Sheet
summary: A step-by-step chain from a prompting event through thoughts, feelings and actions to the outcome.
goal: Use it to help a client see the links in a pattern and where a skill could fit.
body_md: Map one recent moment in small steps, and keep the tone curious rather than critical. Mark the links where a different skill could have changed the chain. Complete it in session first, and use shorter chains for homework.

summary: A menu built from the IMPROVE skills so a client can pick one for a hard moment.
goal: Use it to help a client get through a painful moment without making it worse.
body_md: Go through the letters one by one and have the client write an idea of their own for each. Rehearse one in the room. Remind them that these skills help them get through a moment and do not solve the underlying problem.

title: Emotion Mind and Reasonable Mind Sort
summary: A sorting page that places a client's recent thoughts and urges under emotion, reasonable or wise mind.
goal: Use it to help a client tell which state is driving their choices.
body_md: Take three recent decisions and sort the thoughts behind each. Ask what the client would have done from each state. No state is bad; the point is noticing which one is steering. Practice finding the overlap that wise mind uses.

title: Both-And Dialectic Statements
summary: A page for rewriting either-or sentences into both-and ones that hold two truths.
goal: Use it to help a client loosen rigid thinking by holding two things at once.
body_md: Start with simple examples such as 'I am tired and I can keep going.' Then have the client rewrite a sentence from their own week. Watch for 'but' creeping back in and invite 'and.' Share a few aloud so the practice feels shared.

title: Mindfulness What and How Skills Log
summary: A log that records which what skill and how skill the client practiced and what they noticed.
goal: Use it to help a client build a habit of practicing core mindfulness skills.
body_md: Review the what skills (observe, describe, participate) and the how skills (nonjudgmentally, one-mindfully, effectively) together. Ask for one short practice a day. In follow-up, focus on what the client noticed instead of how well they did.

title: Dreams Within Conflict Talk
summary: A guide for each partner to share the dream or story underneath a recurring disagreement.
goal: Use it to help partners hear what a stuck conflict means to each of them.
body_md: Choose one gridlocked topic. Each partner takes a turn as speaker while the other listens and asks curious questions. The listener does not fix or defend. Each partner fills in their own half before the conversation and shares only what they choose.

summary: A guide for partners to take turns talking about outside stress while the other simply supports.
goal: Use it to help partners turn toward each other about stress that is not about them.
body_md: Each partner gets about fifteen minutes as speaker. The listener's job is to understand, not to fix. Coach them to ask open questions and to show they are on the speaker's side. Watch for advice slipping in and name it kindly.

title: Love Map Question Deck
summary: A set of open questions partners ask each other to learn and update what they know about each other.
goal: Use it to help partners rebuild curiosity about each other's inner world.
body_md: Have the partners pick cards in turn and answer for themselves first. Notice which questions surprise them. If a topic is tender, let either partner pass. Ask what they want to remember about each other this week.

title: Bids Tally for Turning Toward
summary: A tally sheet where partners notice small bids for connection and how they answered.
goal: Use it to help partners notice and respond to everyday bids for attention.
body_md: Explain a bid as any small attempt to connect, such as a comment or a touch. Each partner tallies their own bids and their responses during the week. Review without scorekeeping against each other and pick one bid to answer more often.

title: Aftermath of a Fight Review
summary: A guided review for after an argument: what each felt, what was heard and what each wants to own.
goal: Use it to help partners learn from a rupture and repair after it.
body_md: Wait until both partners are calm. Each partner shares their own feelings and perceptions in turn while the other listens without arguing the facts. Close with what each owns and one change for next time. Stop if either partner becomes flooded.

fields.label: Partner A: how I felt and what I needed
Partner B: how I felt and what I needed

title: Worry Stone Painting Craft
summary: A craft where a child paints a smooth stone to hold during worried moments.
goal: Use it to give a child a calming object they made themselves.
body_md: Let the child pick stone and colors and talk about what a worry stone could do. Show how to rub it and breathe slowly. Afterward, give the parent the idea to keep a basket of stones at home and to practice the breathing with their child.

summary: A booklet of coupons a child decorates and gives to family members for acts of kindness.
goal: Use it to help a child practice noticing and doing kind things.
body_md: The child cuts, folds and decorates a small booklet and writes or draws kind acts on each coupon. The parent chooses one coupon to redeem at home and says what they enjoyed. Keep the focus on joy and connection, not on being good.

fields.label: A kind thing I can do for someone at home

title: Cardboard Calm Castle Build
summary: A build-it project where a child makes a cozy cardboard castle for calming down.
goal: Use it to help a child make a quiet place and a plan for using it.
body_md: The child builds a small castle from a box and decorates it with calming items of their choice. Practice going in, taking slow breaths and coming out. The parent agrees not to send them there as a punishment and shows how to offer it with a gentle invitation.

title: Emotion Monster Puppet Craft
summary: A puppet craft where a child makes a monster with a face for a feeling and gives it a voice.
goal: Use it to help a child name a feeling and talk about it through a puppet.
body_md: The child makes a puppet from a paper bag or sock and picks a feeling for it. Play short scenes where the monster says what it needs. Follow the child's lead. The parent practices answering the puppet kindly and not fixing the feeling.

title: Bubble Breathing Play Plan
summary: A play plan using bubbles to practice slow, steady breathing.
goal: Use it to teach a child to slow their breath through play.
body_md: Blow bubbles together and show that a slow breath makes big, steady bubbles while a fast one pops them. Then practice pretend bubbles with no wand. The parent learns the game and offers it at calm times first so it is familiar when needed.

title: Values Bidding Table Game
summary: A group game in which players bid play money on values and then talk about their choices.
goal: Use it to help players discover what they prize by choosing what to spend on.
body_md: Give each player the same amount of play money and a list of values to bid on. Run each round briefly. In the debrief, ask what they bid on, what they let go and what it felt like to choose. No bid is right, and players may pass.

fields.label: The values I bid on
One I wanted but did not get

One way I can honor a value this week

title: Thought or Fact Buzzer Round
summary: A quick team game in which players buzz in to label statements as thoughts, facts or both.
goal: Use it to help players practice separating thoughts from facts.
body_md: Read a mix of statements aloud. Teams take turns buzzing in to say thought or fact and why. Include a few that are tricky. In the debrief, invite players to share one thought of their own they can now sort out.

fields.label: A statement that was hard to sort
A thought of mine I treat as a fact
How I can check a thought
What I will do next time I notice it

title: Skill Memory Match Game
summary: A card-matching game that pairs a hard situation with a coping skill that fits.
goal: Use it to help players link everyday problems with skills they can use.
body_md: Make two sets of cards, one of situations and one of skills. Players take turns flipping two cards and explain how the skill could help if they find a match. Players may suggest their own skills. In the debrief, ask which skills they would use.

fields.label: A match I made and why it fits
A skill I have used before
A skill I want to try
A situation I want to be ready for

title: Pass the Problem Story Circle
summary: A group story game where each player adds a step to help a character solve a problem.
goal: Use it to help players practice problem solving and perspective taking.
body_md: Start a story with a character facing a problem. Each player adds one sentence in turn about what the character feels or does. After a round, discuss what helped. The leader keeps the problem light and avoids stories that mirror a player's situation.

fields.label: The character's problem in my words
What I added to the story
The idea I liked best from someone else
What I could try if I had that problem

title: Zone Hop Feelings Floor Game
summary: A floor game where players hop to a colored zone that matches a feeling and share a time they felt it.
goal: Use it to help players name feelings and notice how they change.
body_md: Lay out four colored sheets for different feeling zones. Call out a scenario and have players hop to the zone that fits. Invite them to share, but let them pass. Close by asking each player what helps them move between zones.

fields.label: A zone I landed on and why
A time I felt that way

title: Window of Steadiness Daily Check
summary: A daily check of how settled the client's body feels and which supports help them stay in range.
goal: Use it to help a client notice when they are steady and what helps them stay there.
body_md: This is a stabilizing check-in, not a place to describe what happened. Have the client rate steadiness and note what supports helped. Review it together for patterns in the day. If numbers climb, shift to grounding in the session.

fields.label: How settled my body felt today, zero to ten

title: Safety Versus Reminder Thought Check
summary: A thought check that separates a reminder of the past from danger in the present moment.
goal: Use it to help a client tell a reminder apart from what is happening now.
body_md: Keep this in the present. Ask the client to name what in the room tells them they are safe now, and to note the reminder without retelling events. Stop and ground if the client drifts into details. Complete it together before sending it home.

fields.label: What reminded me today, in a few words
What my mind told me it meant
What tells me I am safe right now
A kinder thought I can hold right now

title: Making Room While Staying Oriented Practice
summary: A short practice for noticing a memory or feeling without pushing it away, paced by the client.
goal: Use it to help a client make a little room for hard inner experience while staying present.
body_md: Frame this as noticing, not retelling. The client keeps eyes open and stays oriented to the room, naming five things they see. Stop at any sign of overwhelm. Make sure they leave grounded and agree on what support is available between sessions.

fields.label: Where I felt the reminder in my body
What I did to make room for it
What I saw in the room to stay present
What I want my life to be about

title: Self-Soothing Senses Plan for Trauma Reminders
summary: A plan matching each of the five senses with a soothing item for moments after a reminder.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare calming steps for after a reminder shows up.
body_md: Build the plan in a calm moment and try each sense in session. Choose items that feel safe and pleasant to the client, which can differ from what the clinician expects. Help them place the plan where they can find it quickly. If risk comes up, use 988 (call or text) and complete safety planning in session.

fields.label: Something I can see that calms me
A sound that settles me
A scent that feels safe

title: Grounding Card Draw Round
summary: A card game with grounding prompts that players draw and try one at a time.
goal: Use it to help players practice grounding in a low-pressure group setting.
body_md: Make cards with simple grounding prompts such as naming colors or feeling feet on the floor. Players draw a card, try it and say how it felt. They can pass. Keep it light and present-focused. In the debrief, ask which prompts to keep.

fields.label: A card I drew and tried
What I noticed in my body

title: Anxiety Body Map and Early Signals
summary: A body outline where the client marks where anxiety shows up and which signals come first.
goal: Use it to help a client spot early signals of anxiety so they can respond sooner.
body_md: Hand over a body outline and have the client color where they feel anxiety and add words. Ask which sign comes first. Early signals give them a window to use a skill. Return to the map over a few sessions to see if it changes.

The first sign I notice

title: Uncertainty Experiment Planner
summary: A planner for choosing a small uncertain situation, predicting what will happen and checking afterward.
goal: Use it to help a client practice tolerating not knowing.
body_md: Pick something small where the client usually seeks certainty. Write the prediction, run the experiment and compare. Keep the stakes low at first. Ask what the client learned about getting through not knowing, rather than about whether the prediction came true.

title: Anxiety as a Radio Practice
summary: A practice of letting anxiety play in the background like a radio while doing something that matters.
goal: Use it to help a client act on values while anxiety is present.
body_md: Describe anxiety as a radio that plays whether they like it or not. Have the client choose a small task that matters to them and do it with the radio on. Ask what they noticed about turning toward the task. Avoid promising the radio will go quiet.
