title: Interpersonal Effectiveness Starter Script Page
summary: A page for drafting short conversation starters and follow-ups using DBT skills.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare a few simple lines for starting and ending talks.
body_md: Draft two openers, two follow-up questions and one way to leave gracefully. Practice them aloud with you playing the other person. Use GIVE skills to keep it warm. Clients often over-prepare; aim for lines that sound like them and a plan to use one this week.

fields.label: An opener in my voice
A follow-up question
A way to show interest
A way to end the chat kindly
When I will try one

title: Courage Chart for Social Steps
summary: A child and parent build a chart of small social steps and add stickers or drawings as each is tried.
goal: Use it to help a child take small, playful social steps with a parent cheering them on.
body_md: The child and parent draw a path of steps, from waving to a neighbor to asking someone to play, and pick the first. Parent cheers effort, not outcome, and does not push. Reward trying, whatever happens. Review the chart weekly and add steps the child chooses.

fields.label: The first step on my path
The step I want to reach
How my body feels when I try
Who cheers for me
What I will draw when I try a step

title: Continuing Bonds Ideas Page
summary: A page for ways a client can stay connected to someone who died while living on.
goal: Use it to help a client find ways to keep a bond with someone they lost.
body_md: Ask what the client wants to keep of the person, such as a recipe, a song or a saying, and what they might do with it. Grief has no schedule; accept sadness as part of the work. Choose one small act for the coming week and revisit it next time.

fields.label: Something I want to keep of them
A way I could honor it
A ritual I would like
Who I could share this with
One thing I will do this week

title: Unfinished Business Letter Page
summary: A page for writing a letter to the person who died to say what was left unsaid, kept in the client's hands.
goal: Use it to help a client say what was left unsaid, at their pace and in their own words.
body_md: The client may write what they wish they had said, and does not have to share it. You can offer to listen to any part they choose. Check how they feel after writing and give time to settle. For complicated relationships, go slowly and let the client set the pace.

fields.label: What I wish I had said
What I want them to know
What I am still carrying
What I would like to let go of
How I feel after writing

title: Making Room for Sorrow and Love Practice
summary: A practice that holds sorrow as a sign of love and chooses a small valued action.
goal: Use it to help a client make room for grief while still acting on what matters.
body_md: Invite the client to notice where sorrow sits in the body and what it says about what they loved. Link it to a small action in honor of that love. Avoid steering the client away from pain; let the practice hold both. Check how the client feels at the end.

fields.label: What I loved about them
Where I feel sorrow in my body
What the sorrow says about love
A small action in honor of them
What I need to take care of myself

title: Riding the Grief Wave With Skills Card
summary: A card with skills to use when waves of grief arrive: self-soothe, ride, reach out.
goal: Use it to give a client skills for waves of grief.
body_md: Make a card with a self-soothing step, a way to ride the wave without fighting it and a person to reach out to. Practice one in session. Waves can arrive without warning, so make the card portable. If a client mentions thoughts of ending their life, talk it through in session; 988 can be called or texted.

fields.label: A self-soothing step
A way to ride the wave
A person I can reach out to
What I tell myself during a wave
If I feel unsafe, I can call or text 988

title: Memory Box Decorating Craft
summary: A child decorates a box and fills it with drawings and small objects that remind them of someone they lost.
goal: Use it to give a child a drawn and built way to remember someone.
body_md: The child decorates a box and fills it with items and drawings. The parent shares a memory and listens to the child's. Let the child lead and stop when they want. Children grieve in bursts and play in between, which is normal. If a child discloses harm, follow your reporting duties.

fields.label: Who this box is for
Something I remember
Something I put in the box
How I feel when I look at it
Who I can show it to

title: Relationship Patterns Reflection Page
summary: A page for noticing repeated patterns across relationships and what the client brings to them.
goal: Use it to help a client notice patterns across their relationships.
body_md: Ask the client to describe two or three relationships and look for common threads in how they start, how conflict goes and how they end. Hold it lightly; patterns are not blame. Ask which pattern they would like to change first and what small step would test it.

fields.label: A relationship that mattered
How it started and how conflict went
A thread that repeats
What I bring to it
A pattern I want to change
A small step this week

title: Assumptions About Their Motives Check
summary: A sheet for checking assumptions about why someone acted and testing alternatives.
goal: Use it to help a client check assumptions about other people's intentions.
body_md: Pick a recent moment the client read as a slight, then list other possible reasons. Ask how they could find out and what they would do with the answer. Most clients end up planning a conversation. Rehearse the opening sentence in session.

fields.label: What happened
What I assumed it meant
Other possible reasons
How I could find out
What I will say or do

title: Relationship Values and Actions Page
summary: A page linking what a client values in relationships to specific actions this week.
goal: Use it to help a client act on relationship values through small steps.
body_md: Ask what kind of friend, partner or family member the client wants to be and note moments they acted that way. Then plan two actions for the week. Notice where old habits pull them away and ask what they will do. Keep goals within the client's control.

fields.label: The kind of person I want to be in my relationships
A recent moment I lived it
An action for this week
What old habit may show up
What I will do then

title: GIVE and FAST Combined Conversation Card
summary: A card that combines GIVE and FAST skills for a conversation where the relationship and self-respect both matter.
goal: Use it to help a client prepare for a hard conversation with a person they want to keep.
body_md: Prepare one real conversation and write a line for each skill. Rehearse it twice, once smoothly and once with pushback. Ask which part feels hardest, and rehearse that part again. Debrief after the real conversation to see what to adjust.

fields.label: The conversation I need to have
A gentle line for them
A fair line for me
An honest line
What I will do if they push back
How I will care for myself after

title: Repair Attempt Phrases List
summary: Partners build a short list of phrases that help them repair during a disagreement.
goal: Use it to help partners agree on repair phrases that actually work for them.
body_md: Each partner writes phrases that would help them de-escalate, such as "can we take a break" or "I am sorry for my tone." Share the lists and choose five that both will accept. Practice using one in a mild disagreement in session. Agree how to receive a repair without saying "too late."

fields.label: Partner A: phrases that help me soften
Partner B: phrases that help me soften
Five we both accept
How we will receive a repair attempt
When we will practice

title: Trusted Adults and Support Contacts Page
summary: A page for listing safe people, what each can help with and how to reach them.
goal: Use it to help a client map people who can support them and how to contact them.
body_md: Keep the page in the present: who feels safe, what each person can help with and how to reach them. Do not ask for details of what happened. Include a professional line and 988 by call or text. If a minor discloses abuse, follow your reporting duties and explain them in plain words.

fields.label: People who feel safe to me
What each person can help with
How I can reach them
A professional or helpline I can contact
If I feel unsafe, I can call or text 988
Who I will tell about this page

title: Self-Blame Fact Check Without Details
summary: A sheet for examining self-blame thoughts using present-day facts about responsibility, without retelling events.
goal: Use it to help a client look at self-blame thoughts without writing about what happened.
body_md: Work only with the thought itself, such as "it was my fault," and ask what the client would say to a friend who held it. Do not ask for a description of events and do not assign this as homework. Pace it and stop to ground if distress rises. Responsibility lies with the person who harmed.

fields.label: The thought I notice
How strongly I believe it from 0 to 100
What I would say to a friend who thought this
What I notice in my body
A steadier thought for today
What helps me ground now

title: Choosing Safety and Connection Values Page
summary: A page that links safety, connection and care to small choices a client can make today.
goal: Use it to help a client choose small steps toward safety and connection at their own pace.
body_md: Ask what safety and connection mean to the client now and one small step that fits. Keep the focus on the present and the client's choice. They set the pace and can say no to any part. Check in on how they are feeling and ground before closing.

fields.label: What safety means to me today
A person or place that feels connected
One small choice I can make today
What makes it hard
What helps me feel steady

title: Boundaries and Saying No Practice Cards
summary: Cards for practicing short sentences that set a boundary, with a plan for support afterward.
goal: Use it to help a client rehearse boundaries in small, safe steps.
body_md: Practice low-stakes boundary lines first and let the client choose the wording. Use DEAR MAN where it fits. Include a plan for support afterward. Never require the client to practice with someone who is unsafe; rehearse with you or a safe person only.

fields.label: A small boundary I can set
The words I will use
Who I will practice with
What I will do if I feel uneasy
Who I can talk to afterward

title: My Body Safety Circles Drawing
summary: A child draws circles of people by how close they may be and learns the body safety rules.
goal: Use it to help a child learn body safety rules and who to tell, using drawing.
body_md: The child draws circles from closest to farthest and places people in them, then practices the rules: my body is mine, I can say no and I can tell a trusted adult. Remind parents the child is not to blame. Reporting duties apply if a child discloses anything; follow your agency's steps and tell the child and parent what will happen next.

fields.label: People in my closest circle
People I know but am less close to
Strangers
The grown-ups I can tell
What I can say if I feel uncomfortable

title: Coping Toolbox Builder by Feeling
summary: A page that sorts coping skills into boxes for different feelings and situations.
goal: Use it to help a client build a toolbox with the right tools for each feeling.
body_md: Ask which feelings come up most and what the client does now, then fill in a few tools for each one. Note which tools are only available at home. Have them try one tool from each box before the next session and bring back what worked.

fields.label: A feeling that comes up a lot
Tools I already use for it
A new tool to try
A tool I can use anywhere
What I noticed after trying it

title: Believable Coping Statement Cards
summary: Index cards with realistic coping statements for hard moments, written in the client's own voice.
goal: Use it to help a client write coping thoughts that sound believable to them.
body_md: Collect coping statements the client believes at least a little, not slogans. Test each by saying it aloud and rating how believable it feels. Adjust the wording until it rings true. Keep the cards where they will be used, such as a phone note.

fields.label: A hard moment I face
What I tell myself now
A coping thought I could believe
How believable it is from 0 to 100
Where I will keep it

title: Workable or Not Coping Review
summary: A review of current coping strategies and whether each one works in the short and long run.
goal: Use it to help a client check whether their habits move them toward what matters.
body_md: List the client's go-to strategies and ask for each: does it help in the moment, and where does it lead over months. No strategy is bad in itself; it is a question of fit. Pick one to keep, one to adjust and one to add.

fields.label: A coping habit I use a lot
What it does for me right now
Where it leads over time
Does it move me toward what matters
One I will keep, adjust or add

title: Accumulate Positives Daily Menu
summary: A menu of everyday positives for building resilience before hard moments hit.
goal: Use it to help a client build daily positives to buffer stress.
body_md: Build a menu of small, regular positives such as a walk, a call or music. The client picks one each day and logs it. Distinguish coping in the moment from building a buffer in advance. Review next session which items fit easily into the week.

fields.label: Small positives I enjoy
Ones I can do in ten minutes
One I will do each day
What got in the way
What I noticed about my mood

title: Act-Out-a-Skill Team Relay
summary: A relay game where teams act out coping skills for others to guess, then name when they would use them.
goal: Use it to give a group a fun way to review and remember coping skills.
body_md: Prepare cards with coping skills and have teams act them out. After each guess, the actor names a moment they could use it. Keep it light and let anyone pass. Debrief which skills were new and which they want to try this week.

fields.label: A skill I recognized
A skill I want to try
A moment I could use it
What I learned from the others
My pick for this week

title: Avoidance Map for Feared Situations
summary: A map of places and activities a client avoids and what that avoidance costs.
goal: Use it to help a client see how avoiding a fear shapes daily life.
body_md: Ask the client to list what they avoid or arrange around, including small workarounds. Rate how much each limits them. This is a starting point for a ladder, not a push to face things. Choose one item that matters most to the client.

fields.label: Things I avoid because of this fear
Workarounds I use
What it costs me
What I would do if I were not afraid
The item that matters most

title: Fear Feared Outcome and Coping Page
summary: A page that pairs the feared outcome with the client's plan for coping if it happened.
goal: Use it to help a client think through what they fear and how they could cope.
body_md: Name the feared outcome clearly, rate how likely it feels and then spend time on how the client would cope. Plan a small exposure step to check the prediction. Keep steps within the client's agreement; they choose the pace and can pause.

fields.label: What I fear will happen
How likely it feels from 0 to 100
How I would cope if it did
A small step to test it
What I found out

title: Fear and Direction Willingness Page
summary: A page for choosing a valued activity that sits near a fear and making room for the fear on the way.
goal: Use it to help a client choose willingness for the sake of something they care about.
body_md: Ask what the fear keeps the client from, and why it matters. Pick a step and rate willingness. Name the thoughts and sensations that come along. Offer the step as a choice, not a test, and plan how to acknowledge the fear without arguing with it.

fields.label: What matters to me that the fear blocks
A step toward it
My willingness from 0 to 10
What the fear says
What I will do with it on board

title: Opposite Action Approach Steps Card
summary: A card with small approach steps that act opposite to the urge to avoid when avoiding does not fit the facts.
goal: Use it to help a client approach a feared thing in small steps.
body_md: Check the facts together and, if the fear does not fit the danger, plan a step opposite to avoidance. Use body posture and a confident voice as part of acting opposite. Rehearse in imagination first. Review how it went and adjust the step size.

fields.label: The fear and the urge to avoid
Does the fear fit the facts
A small approach step
Body posture I will use
How I will reward myself

title: Brave Explorer Passport Craft
summary: A child makes a passport and collects stamps for each small step toward a feared thing, with a parent as guide.
goal: Use it to give a child a playful record of small, brave steps.
body_md: The child decorates a passport and draws small steps from far away to near. Each try earns a stamp, whatever the result. The parent models calm and does not push or trick the child. Go at the child's pace and review weekly.

fields.label: The thing I want to get closer to
My first small step
How I feel in my body
What my parent will do
What my stamp will look like

title: What My Body Lets Me Do Page
summary: A page that lists activities and moments a client's body makes possible.
goal: Use it to help a client notice what their body does for them rather than how it looks.
body_md: Ask the client to list everyday things their body makes possible, such as hugging someone or walking to a favorite place. Do not discuss appearance, size or shape. Notice any resistance and keep the page about function and experience. Add to it each week.

fields.label: Things my body lets me do
A moment this week I was glad of my body
A person I can hug, walk or dance with
What I appreciate on a hard day
One more I will add this week

title: Mirror and Media Thought Check Sheet
summary: A sheet for noticing thoughts that rise from social media or the mirror and testing them.
goal: Use it to help a client examine thoughts triggered by media or mirrors.
body_md: Ask what the client sees and thinks when scrolling or passing a mirror and how it shifts their mood. Look at which accounts leave them feeling worse and which help. Test small changes, such as muting accounts. Keep the focus on thoughts and feelings, never on measuring or comparing the body.

fields.label: Where I notice these thoughts
What I tell myself
How it changes my mood
A kinder, fairer thought
A small change I can try with my media

title: Living Fully Beyond Appearance Practice
summary: A practice for choosing actions that fit values even when appearance thoughts show up.
goal: Use it to help a client act on values while appearance thoughts are present.
body_md: Ask what the client has skipped because of appearance thoughts and what they would do if the thoughts could come along. Choose one activity and plan it. Practice noticing the thoughts as thoughts. Revisit how it went and what mattered most.

fields.label: Something I have skipped because of these thoughts
Why it matters to me
The thoughts that show up
What I will do with them along
When I will do it

title: Self-Validation and Opposite Action for Hiding
summary: A page that validates the urge to hide and plans an opposite action that fits the facts.
goal: Use it to help a client respond kindly to urges to hide and take a small step out.
body_md: Validate the feeling first and then check whether hiding serves the client's goals. Plan one small opposite action, such as going to an event for twenty minutes. Include a kind sentence to say to oneself. Review how it went and adjust the step.

fields.label: The urge to hide and when it shows up
A validating sentence to myself
Does hiding help my goals
A small opposite action
How I will care for myself afterward

title: Compliments Beyond Looks Group Game
summary: A group game where players give and receive compliments about character, effort and actions.
goal: Use it to give a group practice noticing and naming what is good beyond appearance.
body_md: Deal prompt cards such as "someone who is a good listener" and have players offer a compliment on character or action only, never looks. Debrief how it felt to receive them and how to keep noticing outside the group. Players may pass at any time.

fields.label: A compliment I gave
A compliment I received
What it felt like to receive it
A quality I like in myself
How I will notice it this week

title: Energy Spending and Refilling Week Planner
summary: A one-page planner for spending and refilling energy across a week of activities.
goal: Use it to help a client see where energy goes and plan realistic rest.
body_md: Have the client list the week's commitments and rate how draining or refilling each feels, then look together for days that are overbooked. The planner is a conversation starter, not a verdict; let the client decide what to move, drop or protect, and revisit it next session.

fields.label: The activities that take the most energy this week
The activities that give energy back
A day that looks overbooked
One thing I could move, shorten or drop
One refill I will protect this week

title: Values-Based Weekly Calendar Review
summary: A calendar review that compares how a client spent their week with what matters to them.
goal: Use it to help a client notice gaps between their time and their stated values.
body_md: Ask the client to bring their real calendar and name two or three values before filling in the sheet. Look for matches and gaps without judgment; the aim is a small adjustment the client chooses, not a perfect schedule. Keep the changes small enough to try this week.

fields.label: Two or three things that matter most to me
Where my week matched them
Where my week did not match them
One small change I am willing to try
How I will know I tried it

title: Weekend Reset Menu Builder
summary: A menu a client builds of restful, social and useful things to choose from on days off.
goal: Use it to help a client plan days off so they feel restored rather than drained.
body_md: Have the client sort ideas into rest, connection and useful chores, then choose one from each column for the coming weekend. Look at whether the plan leaves any open time. Clients often over-schedule days off or leave them empty; ask what restores them and let them adjust the plan.

fields.label: Things that help me rest
Things that help me connect with others
Chores I would like off my list
My picks for this weekend
What I will do if the plan falls apart

title: Small Wins Capture Log
summary: A daily log for recording small things that went right, however minor.
goal: Use it to help a client build the habit of noticing progress that is easy to overlook.
duration: Five minutes daily for two weeks
body_md: Introduce it as a place to write the ordinary, not the impressive: a call returned, a walk taken, a hard moment handled a little differently. Review the log together and ask what the client's wins say about what they can do. Keep the entries short so the habit stays easy.

fields.label: Today's small win
What I did to make it happen
Who or what helped
What it tells me about myself
The win I would like to repeat tomorrow

title: Ten-Ten-Ten Decision Timeline Sheet
summary: A timeline sheet that asks how a choice will feel in ten minutes, ten months and ten years.
goal: Use it to help a client look past the pull of the moment when making a choice.
body_md: Name the decision and have the client write how each option is likely to feel at each time frame. Differences across the three often show the pull of short-term relief. Let the client decide in their own time; the sheet is a way to see the choice from further away.

fields.label: The decision I am facing
How each option feels in ten minutes
How each option may feel in ten months
How each option may feel in ten years
What I notice looking across all three

title: Rigid Rules to Flexible Preferences Rewrite
summary: A sheet for turning must and should rules into preferences that leave room for exceptions.
goal: Use it to help a client loosen rules about themselves that leave no room for being human.
body_md: The client writes rules they hold, such as I must never make mistakes, and rewrites each as a preference, such as I would like to do well and I can recover when I do not. Ask what the rule is meant to protect and what it costs. Practice the rewrite on a recent event.

fields.label: A rule I hold for myself
What the rule is meant to protect
What it costs me
The same rule as a preference
How I will use the new version this week

title: Prediction Tally Weekly Scoreboard
summary: A scoreboard where a client tallies predictions against what actually happened.
goal: Use it to help a client see over time how often predicted outcomes come true.
body_md: Each day the client writes a prediction, what happened and a tick for whether it came true. At the end of the week add up the ticks. The tally is a way to look at the pattern, and clients are often surprised. Discuss which predictions were closest and why.

fields.label: Today's prediction
What actually happened
Did it come true? Yes, partly or no
Which predictions were closest
What the tally tells me this week

title: Cognitive Flexibility Perspective Wheel
summary: A wheel of other viewpoints a client can try on in a stuck moment.
goal: Use it to help a client generate more than one reading of a situation.
body_md: Draw a circle with spokes for viewpoints such as a friend, a future self, a neutral observer and someone who cares about the client. The client writes how each might read the same event. The goal is more options, not a correct answer; ask which viewpoint feels most useful and why.

fields.label: The situation and my first reading of it
How a good friend might see it
How I might see it a year from now
How a neutral observer might see it
The reading I want to keep in mind

title: Worry Time Appointment Tracker
summary: A tracker for postponing worries to a set daily appointment and reviewing them there.
goal: Use it to help a client practice setting worries aside until a chosen time.
body_md: Agree on a fifteen-minute window that is not near bedtime. Through the day the client jots a few words for each worry and returns to what they were doing; at the appointment they read the list and sort which worries need a step. Expect the first days to feel awkward.

fields.label: The time I chose for worry time
Worries I wrote down today in a few words
Which ones still matter at worry time
A step I can take on one of them
What happened when I postponed a worry

title: Pre-Event Rumination Interrupt Sheet
summary: A sheet for noticing and redirecting rehearsing and replaying before a feared event.
goal: Use it to help a client shift attention from rehearsing worries to the task ahead.
body_md: The client lists what they replay or rehearse before an event, what it does for them and what it costs in time and mood. Then they choose a task-focused activity to switch to and a time limit. Practice the switch in session with a recent example and review how it went.

fields.label: What I replay or rehearse before an event
What it does for me
What it costs me
What I can switch to instead
My time limit for rehearsing

title: Compass and Weather Report Values Page
summary: A page that treats feelings as weather and values as a compass for the day's direction.
goal: Use it to help a client keep heading toward their values whatever the inner weather.
body_md: The client describes today's inner weather and then the compass direction they want to travel. Ask what they can do in rain that still points the same way. Weather changes whether or not it is acted on; the compass stays steady. Revisit it each session.

fields.label: Today's inner weather
My compass direction
What the weather tells me to do
What I can do that points my compass way
A small step for today

title: Thought Radio Volume Exercise
summary: An exercise that treats thoughts as background radio the client can turn down but not off.
goal: Use it to help a client notice thoughts as sounds while they get on with what matters.
body_md: Ask the client to imagine a radio that plays their thoughts and to give it a station name. Have them do a small task with the radio playing. Notice that they can act without turning the radio off. Ask what the radio says most and how it might sound with a silly voice.

fields.label: The name of my thought radio station
What it plays most often
What I did with it playing in the background
What changed when I gave it a silly voice
Where I could use this this week

title: Values Ruler Rating Page
summary: A page where a client rates how closely each area of life matches their values.
goal: Use it to help a client spot where actions and values are furthest apart.
body_md: The client picks several life areas, such as family, work, health and friends, writes how much each matters and how closely they have lived it this week. The gap is where to put small steps. Do not use it to grade the client; it shows where to look first.

fields.label: Life areas that matter to me
How much each matters, 0 to 10
How closely I lived it this week, 0 to 10
The area with the biggest gap
One small step for that area

title: Mindful Dishwashing Everyday Task Practice
summary: A practice of bringing full attention to one ordinary task such as washing dishes.
goal: Use it to help a client practice present-moment attention in daily life.
body_md: Choose a routine task and have the client notice the temperature, the sounds and the movements for a few minutes, and bring attention back when it drifts. The practice is about the returning. Review what pulled them away and what they noticed.

fields.label: The task I chose
What I noticed through my senses
What pulled my attention away
How I brought it back
Another task I could try

title: Obstacle Cards for Valued Plans
summary: A set of cards pairing likely obstacles with ways to carry on toward a valued goal.
goal: Use it to help a client expect the obstacles that come between a plan and action.
body_md: Name the valued action and have the client write cards for the obstacles inside them, such as thoughts and feelings, and outside, such as time and tiredness, each with a way to carry on. Rehearse one card aloud and agree on when it will be tried.

fields.label: The valued action I plan
An obstacle inside me
How I will carry on with it
An obstacle outside me
How I will deal with that one

title: Apologizing Without Over-Apologizing Script
summary: A script for a short, honest apology that does not take on blame that is not the client's.
goal: Use it to help a client apologize clearly when it is warranted, and stop when it is not.
body_md: Have the client sort things they apologize for into those that are theirs and those that are not. For the first group, write a short apology: what happened, my part and what I will do. For the second, practice other phrases. Role-play a few.

fields.label: Something I tend to apologize for
Is it mine to apologize for?
A short apology with my part and what I will do
A phrase to use when it is not mine
Who I will practice with

title: Check the Facts Emotion Review
summary: A review sheet that separates the facts of an event from the story and feeling attached to it.
goal: Use it to help a client see whether an emotion fits the facts of what happened.
body_md: Have the client name the emotion, the event that set it off, and the interpretation they made, then look at which parts are observable facts. Ask whether the intensity matches the facts. Do not rush to say the feeling is wrong; validate it first, then look at the facts.

fields.label: The emotion and how strong it is, 0 to 100
The event that set it off, only the facts
The story I told myself about it
Facts that fit the story and facts that do not
Whether my emotion still fits the facts

title: Coping Ahead for Hard Acceptance Moments Card
summary: A card for rehearsing in advance how to accept a hard moment you cannot change.
goal: Use it to help a client picture a hard moment and rehearse accepting it.
body_md: The client names a situation ahead that they cannot change, writes what will be hard, and rehearses in imagination how they will accept and cope, with a skill for each step. Practice once in session and adjust after the real event.

fields.label: A situation ahead I cannot change
What will be hardest
How I will accept it in the moment
The skill I will use
How I will care for myself afterward

title: Vacation in the Mind Imagery Card
summary: A card for building a short imagined getaway with sensory detail.
goal: Use it to help a client take a mental break from distress.
body_md: Have the client choose a place, real or imagined, and describe it by sight, sound, smell and touch. Practice a two-minute visit in session and rate distress before and after. If imagery brings up unwanted material, switch to something external. Keep a written script they can read.

fields.label: The place I chose
What I see there
What I hear and smell

title: Dialectics Both-And Reframing Sheet
summary: A sheet for holding two seemingly opposite truths at once instead of picking a side.
goal: Use it to help a client loosen all-or-nothing thinking by finding the both-and.
body_md: Have the client write a stuck either-or statement and then rewrite it with and. For example, I am doing my best and I want to do better. Explore how it feels to hold both. Clients who feel invalidated by the rewrite may need the first side acknowledged on its own before the second is added.

title: Weekly State of the Home Check-In
summary: A short weekly check-in where both partners share what is working and what needs attention.
goal: Use it to give partners a predictable time to talk about the relationship calmly.
body_md: Each partner fills in the sheet alone, then they take turns reading answers while the other listens without rebutting. Start with appreciations. Coach them to keep one request each, phrased as something to do, and to stop at the agreed time even if topics are left over.

Partner B: something I appreciated this week

title: Complaint Versus Criticism Sorting Cards
summary: Cards that sort statements into complaints about an action and criticisms of a person.
goal: Use it to help partners tell the two apart and aim for a complaint.
body_md: Write statements on cards, such as you never help versus I felt alone with the dishes, and sort them into complaint or criticism. Then each partner rewrites a recent criticism as a complaint. Discuss how each version lands.

title: Make-Up Plan After a Fight

goal: Use it to help partners recover after a fight and learn from it.
body_md: Partners write what each needs after a fight, such as space, a hug or an apology, and how long. They agree on a way to reconnect and to talk it through when calm, including what each felt and what each would do differently. Use it after a real argument.

goal: Use it to help partners name shared purpose and values.
body_md: Each partner writes what they hope the relationship stands for, then they compare lists and draft two or three sentences together. Let it be loose and revisable. Ask what they could do this month to live the statement.

title: Six-Minute Daily Debrief Talk
summary: A short daily talk where partners take turns telling about their day while the other listens.
goal: Use it to help partners keep up with each other's lives.
body_md: Each partner gets three minutes to talk about their day while the other listens, asks open questions and does not solve. The aim is connection, not advice. Pick a regular time and place, and review after a week how it felt.

title: Feelings Color Wheel Mobile Craft
summary: A hanging mobile where each color stands for a feeling the child picks.
goal: Use it to help a child match feelings with colors and shapes.
body_md: The child cuts shapes in colors they pick for feelings and hangs them from a hanger. Talk about what each color means and when they felt it. The parent points to a color to ask how things are, and accepts any answer. Keep it playful.

title: Worry Rock Pocket Craft
summary: A small painted rock a child holds to set a worry down.
goal: Use it to give a child something to hold while they name a worry and let go.
body_md: The child paints a rock, names it and tells it a worry before bed or at school. The parent hears it, and then the rock goes on a shelf until morning. The goal is to name and put down, not to solve. Replace the rock with a smaller one in a pocket if useful.

title: Brave Moments Picture Frame Craft
summary: A frame a child decorates around a drawing of a brave thing they did.
goal: Use it to help a child hold on to brave moments they can look back at.
body_md: The child decorates a frame and draws or pastes a picture of something brave they did. The parent writes the child's words underneath. Add new pictures over time and ask the child to look at it before a hard thing.

title: Bubble Blowing Slow Breath Play
summary: A play session where a child blows bubbles slowly to practice long, slow breaths.
goal: Use it to teach a child slow breathing through play.
body_md: Blow bubbles together, noticing that slow breaths make big bubbles and fast ones pop them. Count breaths and talk about when slow breaths could help. The parent practices at calm times, not only in upset moments.

title: Kind Words Superhero Cape Craft
summary: A decorated cape covered in kind and brave words the child chooses.
goal: Use it to help a child collect and wear the good things they and others see in them.
body_md: The child decorates a cloth or paper cape with their superhero name and words for their strengths, adding words the parent or friend offers. At home the parent adds a new word when they notice effort. Keep the focus on actions and character. Let the child wear it at the start of the next session.

Words for what I am good at

title: Emotion Charades Round Robin
summary: A charades game where players act out feelings and guess them.
goal: Use it to help a group practice reading and naming feelings from face and body.
body_md: Write feelings on cards. Each player draws one, acts it out without speaking, and others guess, then everyone says one time they felt it. Rotate turns and let players pass. Debrief which feelings were easy or hard to read and what helped them guess.

title: Skill Bingo for Group Practice
summary: A bingo card of coping skills the group marks off as they try them.
goal: Use it to give a group a playful reason to practice skills between sessions.
body_md: Give each player a card of skills, such as paced breathing, a short walk or naming five things they see. Players mark a square when they try one during the week and share a line about it. Offer a small prize for sharing, not for a full card, so no one feels behind.

fields.label: The skill I tried first
What happened when I tried it

title: Pros and Cons Debate Team Game
summary: A game where two teams argue the pros or cons of a choice and then switch sides.
goal: Use it to help players see both sides of a decision in a playful way.
body_md: Pick a small made-up decision. One team argues for, the other against, then they swap. Debrief which arguments stood out and whether anything changed their mind. Move to a real choice only if a player offers one.

The best argument for
The best argument against

title: Values Auction with Pretend Money
summary: A pretend auction where players bid on values and find out what they care about most.
goal: Use it to help players notice which values they would spend the most on.
body_md: Give each player the same pretend budget and a list of values to bid on, such as family, learning, adventure and health. Run the auction, then ask what they chose and what they gave up. There are no right values. Close by asking how one of the won values could show up this week.

fields.label: The value I spent the most on

What I heard from others that I want to remember

title: Sound Hunt Listening Game
summary: A game where players close their eyes and list every sound they can find.
goal: Use it to help players practice listening and settling attention.
body_md: Ask players to listen for one minute with eyes closed or lowered, counting sounds, then share the list. Try again with a different location. Debrief how attention felt and what it was like to come back when the mind wandered.

fields.label: Sounds I heard close to me
Sounds I heard far away
The sound I liked most

Where I could listen this week

title: Daily Rhythm Steadiness Planner
summary: A planner for placing rest, movement and contact through the day to keep a steady pace.
goal: Use it to help a client build a predictable day that supports steadiness.
body_md: Have the client sketch morning, afternoon and evening with one steadying item in each, such as a walk, a meal or a call, using only present-day routines. Note where the day tends to tip into overload or numbness. Keep the plan small and revisit it weekly.

fields.label: My morning anchor
My afternoon anchor
My evening anchor

What I will change this week

title: Reminder Response Plan Card
summary: A card for what a client does when a present-day reminder pulls their attention away.
goal: Use it to help a client plan a calm response to everyday reminders.
body_md: The client lists everyday reminders, such as a smell or a loud noise, without describing the events behind them. For each they write what they notice in the body, a thought to check and a steadying step. Practice one in session when calm and keep it brief.

fields.label: A reminder that shows up in daily life, named briefly
What I notice in my body
A thought I can check against the present

Who I could contact if it lingers

title: Anchoring in Values During Hard Memories
summary: A page that pairs an anchor in the present with a value the client is moving toward.
goal: Use it to help a client stay connected to what matters when reminders show up.
body_md: Start with the client's values and present-day anchors, never with the content of memories. When a reminder shows up in daily life, they notice it, name it, feel their feet and take one small valued step. Pace carefully, and keep the work in the stabilizing range.

fields.label: Something that matters to me
A reminder that sometimes shows up in daily life, named in a few words

title: Cool Down Sequence After a Hard Moment Card
summary: A card with a short sequence for settling the body and mind after a hard moment.
goal: Use it to help a client settle after a reminder has set off strong reactions.
body_md: Build a short sequence with the client: a cold drink, five slow breaths, naming five things they see, and a small next step. Practice in session when calm. The sequence is for settling after a moment passes and not for revisiting what happened.

fields.label: The first thing I will do to settle
My breathing step
Five things I can see
My next small step
Who I could tell

title: Night Routine and Sleep Partner Plan
summary: A plan for partners to make bedtime and nights feel safer and more restful.
goal: Use it to help partners agree on a bedtime routine and what to do if nights are hard.
body_md: Partners discuss what makes bedtime feel safe, such as light, door position or a wind-down, and what each does if one wakes up unsettled. Agree on a calm response and a way to go back to sleep. Neither partner is asked to share the content of any dream.

fields.label: Partner A: what helps me feel safe at night
Partner B: what helps me feel safe at night
Our bedtime routine
What we do if one of us wakes unsettled
When we will review the plan

title: Worry Volume Knob Cardboard Craft
summary: A cardboard dial a child turns to show how loud a worry feels.
goal: Use it to help a child show and adjust how big a worry feels.
body_md: The child decorates a dial from quiet to loud and turns it for a worry. Together try a breath or a silly voice for the worry and see whether the dial moves. The parent practices asking what number it is today, and does not argue the worry away. Keep it playful.

fields.label: A worry I turned the dial for
The number it started at
What I did to turn it down
What my parent did that helped

title: Uncertainty Dice Tolerance Game
summary: A dice game where players try small uncertain choices and notice how they feel.
goal: Use it to help players practice being unsure and finding they can cope.
body_md: Each player rolls a die to pick a small uncertain task from a list, such as picking a snack blindly or choosing a seat without planning. Then they rate discomfort and what they did. Take turns, and let players pass once. Debrief what they noticed about unsureness rising and falling.

fields.label: The small uncertain task I rolled
How uncomfortable I felt, 0 to 10
What I did while I felt it
What happened in the end

title: Anxiety Day and Night Pattern Calendar
summary: A calendar that tracks when anxiety is higher or lower across the week.
goal: Use it to help a client see patterns by time of day and day of the week.
body_md: The client rates anxiety morning, afternoon and evening on a weekly grid and notes what was happening. Look for peaks and quiet spots, and connect them to sleep, caffeine, plans and people. Plan one change for the highest-risk time.

fields.label: The time of day anxiety is highest
What is going on at that time
The time it is lowest and what is happening

title: Best, Worst and Most Likely Outcome Sheet
summary: A sheet for writing the best, worst and most likely outcomes of a worry.
goal: Use it to help a client look at the whole range of outcomes, not just the worst.
body_md: The client writes the worry, then the best case, the worst case and the most likely case, and how they would cope with each. Often the most likely case is ordinary. Ask what they would do about the worst case and which case they have been living in.

fields.label: The worry
The best case
The worst case

title: Making Room for Anxiety Willingness Practice
summary: A practice page for letting anxiety be present while the client does what matters.
goal: Use it to help a client carry anxiety along instead of waiting for it to leave first.
body_md: Ask the client to choose a valued action that anxiety usually blocks, then to notice the feeling, give it room in the body and take the action anyway. Willingness is a choice, not a feeling. Review what happened without grading it, and talk about what they learned about the cost of waiting.

How I made room for it

title: Pacing Energy on Low Days Plan
summary: A plan for splitting a day's tasks into small blocks with rests on low-energy days.
goal: Use it to help a client do the essentials on low days without burning out.
body_md: The client lists tasks, marks the essentials, and splits them into ten-minute blocks with a rest between. Wise mind decides what can wait. Invite them to track energy before and after. Review what helped and adjust.

fields.label: The essentials for today
How I will split them into blocks

title: Low-Mood Days Partner Plan
summary: A plan for how partners stay connected on days when one has little energy.
goal: Use it to give partners agreed ways to support each other on low-energy days.
body_md: The partner with low mood lists what helps and what feels like pressure; the other shares what they can offer and what they need so they do not burn out. They agree on a few small supports and a check-in word. Frame it as a plan for the days, not a fix for the person.

fields.label: Partner A: what helps on a low day
Partner A: what feels like pressure
Partner B: what I can offer without burning out

title: Sunshine and Cloud Feelings Journal Craft
summary: A small journal where a child draws a sun or cloud for each day and one reason why.
goal: Use it to help a child notice how days feel and what changes them.
body_md: The child decorates a journal and draws a sun, cloud or both each evening with one reason. The parent looks at it with them, listens and notices activities linked to sunny days. Look together for patterns in session. Follow your reporting duties if a child discloses harm.

fields.label: How I decorated my journal

title: Activity Menu Spin and Try Game
summary: A spin-the-wheel game that picks a small activity for a client to try.
goal: Use it to help a group choose and try small activities that lift mood.
body_md: Build a wheel of simple activities the group names, such as stretching, texting a friend or stepping outside. Players spin, try or plan the activity, and report how it felt. Let players re-spin once. Debrief which activities were doable and what made starting easier.

title: Low Day and Better Day Comparison Sheet
summary: A two-column sheet that compares what a low day and a better day looked like.
goal: Use it to help a client spot what changes between low days and better days.
body_md: Have the client describe a recent low day and a recent better day in the same categories: sleep, contact with people, movement, and what they did. Look at what differed and which difference they could influence. If thoughts of ending their life show up, complete the 988 prompt in session; 988 can be called or texted.

A better day: what I did and who I saw

title: Task Chunking Estimate Ladder
summary: A ladder that breaks a big task into rungs and estimates each one.
goal: Use it to help a client see a big task as a series of short, doable pieces.
body_md: The client writes a big task, breaks it into rungs of about fifteen minutes and estimates each. They try a rung and compare. Adjust estimates over time. Celebrate each rung completed and pick the first rung to start today.

title: Starting Before Ready Valued Action Page
summary: A page for taking the first small step on a task even when motivation is missing.
goal: Use it to help a client start a valued task with the feelings of dread or boredom along.
body_md: Name the task, the value behind it, and the feeling that blocks starting. The client picks a two-minute first step and a cue. Remind them that the feeling can come along. Review whether starting happened, and shrink the step if it did not.

fields.label: The task I keep putting off
The value behind it

title: Task-Switching Urge Surfing Card
summary: A card for noticing the urge to switch tasks and riding it out for a few minutes.
goal: Use it to help a client stay with a task a little longer than the urge suggests.
body_md: Name the urge to switch, set a short timer, and have the client breathe and note the urge rising and falling before deciding. Write the distraction on a list for later. Start with five minutes and extend only if it works.

title: Shared Household Systems Planner
summary: A planner where partners set up visible routines for the tasks that slip.
goal: Use it to help partners set up systems so reminders do not turn into nagging.
body_md: List recurring household tasks, who does each, and the system that makes each one visible, such as a shared calendar or a labeled basket. Agree how a reminder is asked for and given, so nobody has to be the nag. Test the system for two weeks and revisit it.

title: Focus Racetrack Game Board
summary: A board a child makes that turns task steps into laps around a track.
goal: Use it to help a child break a task into steps and see progress as they go.
body_md: Draw a racetrack with spaces labeled by steps, such as get backpack or write a sentence. The child moves a token one space per step with a small break after each lap. Explain to the parent that the track is a tool for the task, not a reward for behavior. Adjust step size so success is likely.

title: Urge Surfing Wave Game
summary: A game where players ride out an urge as a wave using breath and movement.
goal: Use it to help players practice staying with an urge as it rises and falls.
body_md: Players imagine an urge as a wave and move a hand up and down in time with their breath, rating the urge as it passes. Take turns describing what they noticed. The point is that urges rise and fall, not that they must be defeated. Debrief where players could use this and who they could call.

title: Free Time Gap Filler Weekly Schedule
summary: A schedule that plans activities for the hours when urges are most likely.
goal: Use it to help a client fill high-risk hours with things that matter to them.
body_md: The client marks the hours of the week when substance use urges tend to rise and chooses an activity or person for each. Include one rewarding thing per day. Review which hours were still hard and adjust the plan.

fields.label: The hours when urges are highest

title: Urge Thoughts Alternatives Sheet
summary: A sheet for catching thoughts that push toward substance use and trying other responses.
goal: Use it to help a client notice urge-related thoughts and choose a response.

goal: Use it to help a client make room for an urge while choosing the direction of their life.

title: Urge Survival Distraction Menu

goal: Use it to help a client get through the peak of an urge without acting on it.

fields.label: Activities that take my full attention
People I can call or text

title: Anger Cooling-Off Agreement

goal: Use it to help partners agree on how to pause a heated moment and come back.

title: Anger Volcano Signs Model Craft

goal: Use it to help players practice noticing anger levels and the steps that cool them.

fields.label: The level I acted out

title: Anger Trigger and Underlying Feeling Log

goal: Use it to help a client see what sits under anger, such as hurt or worry.

goal: Use it to help a client turn unspoken rules into specific, fair requests.

goal: Use it to help a client practice accepting uncertainty in small steps.

goal: Use it to help partners agree on small reductions in accommodating rituals.

goal: Use it to help a child see the bossy thought as separate from themselves.

summary: A card for noticing what the body does and practicing neutral, respectful attention.
